# Testing Definitions

Here are our team’s testing definitions. These definitions allow us to have a common reference for our testing documentation and testing discussions. That said, these definitions are open and flexible.

<aside>
📖 Looking for guides? Take a look at our [Testing Guidelines](Testing Guidelines.md) page.

</aside>

## Quick definitions

---

| Concept | What | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SUT | Short for System Under Test. Refers to the code being tested |  |
| Functional Tests | Focused on validating the behaviour of the system rather than specific implementation. 
More of a “black-box” testing approach. | → Validate high-level behaviour |
| Non-functional Tests | Focused on validating non-functional requirements of the system such as performance, load, and resiliency. |  |
| Interaction/implementation testing | Focused on validating a specific implementation, i.e. interaction of the SUT with the rest of the system.
→ e.g. assert method was called with X
→ e.g. using mock
More of a “white-box” testing approach. | → Sometimes we don’t have other choice, for example when testing an API client |
| State testing | Focused on validating the state of the SUT after the code has been executed
→e.g. after updating an entity, query it and assert it’s state has changed | →To ensure the system transitions to the correct state |
| Test double | A fake implementation of an interface that can be used as a replacement for a dependency of the SUT
→ e.g. an in-memory repository | → To narrow the scope of the SUT
→ To simplify test setup
→ To speedup test execution |
| Sociable Tests | Tests whose dependencies are not test doubles but real productive implementations. 
The exception to the above is the use of test doubles to obey with the requirements of the test size
→ e.g. A unit sociable test may use a test double to mock api calls but still use real implementations of synchronous dependencies | → To increase confidence in assumption |
| Solitary Tests | Tests that use of test doubles to isolate dependencies | → Focus only on concrete behavior
→We try to avoid them |
| Exhaustiveness | How likely is that an undesired change in the SUT will make my test fail |  |
| Fidelity | How likely is that changes outside the SUT will make my test start from incorrect assumptions. |  |

## Test size

A test’s size is determined not by its number of lines of code or number of classes it touches but how it runs, what is it allowed to do and how many resources it consumes.

We identify three kind of tests, *unit, integration* and *E2E*

| Kind | Command | Restrictions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | `yarn test:unit` | → Test and code run in the same process
→ Can’t access network databases or queues |
| Integration | `yarn test:integration` | → Test and code run in the same process
→ Can only access network databases and queues that are owned by the project |
| E2E | `yarn test:e2e` | → Test and code run in different processes
→ There’s no stubbing
→ Can’t be a replacement for unit or integration tests
→ It’s acceptable that additional setup is required to run them |

And the result of enforcing these restrictions makes them share these characteristics 

| Kind | Speed | Determinism | Fidelity | Good for | Bad for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | Fast
(50 ms) | High | Low | → Testing multiple scenarios without affecting latency | →Projects that don’t effectively abstract domain from infrastructure
→ Small projects |
| Integration | Medium
(500 ms) | Medium | Medium | →Testing infrastructure
→Increasing confidence
→Small projects | →Writing too many in large projects |
| E2E | Slow
(50 s) | Low | High | → Providing safety nets for core features
→Interacting with third party APIs | →Writing too many in large projects
→Exhaustive assertions |

## Test scope

Test scope refers to how much code is being validated by a given test. Narrow-scoped tests are designed to validate logic in small, focused part of the code base, like and individual class or method. Large-scoped tests are designed to validate interaction of several distinct parts of the system. 

The following table compares the characteristics of narrow and large tests. However this is not a binary classification, in reality tests will be narrower and larger than others at the same time  

| Scope |   Fidelity | Exhaustiveness | Good for | Bad for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Narrower | Lower | Higher | → Battle testing specific functions
→ Testing repositories
→Testing APIs
→Covering edge cases | →Code that might be refactored |
| Larger | Higher | Lower | → Functional tests
→ Legacy code
→ Covering happy paths | →Exhaustive assertions |

## References & Resources

---

![Fig. 1: Diagram showing different testing boundaries within a codebase. The green boundary represents **low-level**, **implementation** or **functional** **unit** tests. The orange boundary represents **low-level**/**high-level**, **implementation** or **functional** **integration** tests. The blue boundary represents **high-level**, **functional** **end-to-end** tests.](Testing%20Definitions/Untitled.png)

Fig. 1: Diagram showing different testing boundaries within a codebase. The green boundary represents **low-level**, **implementation** or **functional** **unit** tests. The orange boundary represents **low-level**/**high-level**, **implementation** or **functional** **integration** tests. The blue boundary represents **high-level**, **functional** **end-to-end** tests.

[On the Diverse And Fantastical Shapes of Testing](https://martinfowler.com/articles/2021-test-shapes.html)

# Coding Practices

## TypeScript

Integrations are written in [TypeScript](https://github.com/Microsoft/TypeScript), which is a typed version of JavaScript. It allows us to pick up common bugs on compile time rather than runtime, provides a smoother developer experience, and makes it easy for other devs to jump in to the code base.

## Terms

You’ll see terms used across the tooling and documentation that are specific to Busbud. More exist, but can be found further in to the documentation.

- “**BoB**” means “book on Busbud”. It’s an integration that will have the `book`, allowing us to complete a full booking on our product.
- “**BoX**” means “book on external”. It’s an integration where search happens on our product, but the user is redirected to the partners website to complete the booking.
- `scratch` is a folder in [Integrations](How Stuff Works/Integrations.md) where you will spend your time developing, allowing you to write your own test code to use against your integration as it’s being written.

## General Rules

- `snake_case` for variables and arguments, `camelCase` for functions. Both should be well named, not single lettered or anything non descriptive.
- Spaces, not tabs.
- Avoid using `var`, use `let` and `const`.
- Use `async`/`await` where possible, avoid promise chains, and absolutely no callbacks.
- We use [Yarn](https://github.com/yarnpkg/yarn) instead of npm.
- We use native Node promises whenever possible. If there’s something you can’t do with native promises (which should be rare), [Bluebird](http://bluebirdjs.com/docs/getting-started.html) is alright. But don’t use it if you just need `tap`, `fromCallback` or `timeout`! For promise queues you can also check out [p-limit](https://github.com/sindresorhus/p-limit).
- We recommend using native functions from Typescript/Javascript for utilities. The [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/bm/docs/Web/JavaScript) is a great resource. We have a collection of utility functions available in [IntUtils](/tsdocs/modules/_busbud_int_utils_dist.html) that can solve many common programming problems. If you require further capabilities that native functions or IntUtils can not provide, we use [Ramda](http://ramdajs.com/) as a last resort.
- [`AdapterOptions`](/tsdocs/interfaces/_busbud_int_schemas_schemas_adapter.adapteroptions.html) is passed to every single `index.ts` and `api.ts` method. Inside it you’ll find helpful preconfigured functions for making outbound requests, logging, and capturing custom errors.
- We use a wrapped version of [got](https://github.com/sindresorhus/got) called `@busbud/http-client` for making outbound requests. Instead of importing as a module, we provide it as [`options.httpClient`](/tsdocs/interfaces/_busbud_int_schemas_schemas_adapter.adapteroptions.html#requester) to every single integration method as stated above. In other microservices, it’s available as part of the `@busbud/service` package.
- Do not add modules to your project that already have an alternative in use. For example, don’t use Lodash as we already use Ramda. Don’t use `axios` as we already use got, etc.
- Do not hardcode credentials or URLs. You can pass these in the constructor of the integration. Your scratch file comes with a space to pass your config.

## Testing

See the following sub-pages:

[Testing Definitions](Coding Practices/Testing Definitions.md)

[Testing Guidelines](Coding Practices/Testing Guidelines.md)

## Code Reviews

A quick tip. Github comes with three options when submitting a code review: ‘Approve’ (a green tick), ‘Request Changes’ (a red box), and ‘Comment’ (a speech box that looks a bit like this: 💬).

Please **do not** use the ‘Comment’ option. We want to know if you are 100% confident that the code can be merged, and that is a yes/no question that ‘Comment’ does not answer.

If you are at all worried that there might be a bug in a PR, select ‘Request Changes’ and ask about it. You can switch to ‘Approve’ right away once the author has confirmed there’s no problem.

You may be tempted to use the ‘Comment’ option because you think it’s more polite than the ‘Request Changes’ option. Please don’t; we honestly don’t mind.

Useful: we use [Toast](https://busbud.slack.com/apps/AC6M092SD-toast-for-github?tab=more_info) slack app which helps to keep track of pull request updates or code review reminders.

## Architecture

[Decision-Making Models: Layered vs Co-centric vs Vertical Slice](https://www.notion.so/Decision-Making-Models-Layered-vs-Co-centric-vs-Vertical-Slice-1c529aab91998061bb39ee5ae6c01573?pvs=21) 

[Software Design (Use Case vs Domain Driven vs Vertical Slicing)](https://www.notion.so/Software-Design-Use-Case-vs-Domain-Driven-vs-Vertical-Slicing-1c529aab919980c6bfa1eef1f14a743a?pvs=21) 

## Random Tips

- Running `yarn lint` is your friend, and `yarn lint:fix` is even better!
- Be sure to read about all the [modules](Our Services/Modules and Packages.md) Busbud has built to get a proper understanding on how they should be used when writing an integration.

## Logs

When working on integrations, new one, rewrite or simply chasing a bug, logs are your best friends. As such, here are some tools to help you querying them easily.

### The easy way *(if you have a request ID or purchase ID)*

The 2 following commands will output all related requests nicely formatted

- If you have a `request-id`, you can use the following command.

```bash
bb adapter-logs <YourAdapter> <request-id>
```

- If you have a `purchase-id`, you can use the following command.

```bash
bb purchase-logs <purchase-id>
```

<aside>
💡 Use the flag `--preview` for purchases on preview.

</aside>

### Manually querying logs

First, the good old way, doing it by hand.

```bash
bb gcs-logs
```

This command will SSH into a unix environnement where you will get access to every logs organized in folders. One folder for each integration. Nice! Now, you have access to every logs, cool, but how to query them? Let jump to an example.

**Example**

> I want to get the last 10 getDepartureDetails requests from the 1st of April for the J3 integration
> 

```bash
cd j3
cd 2020-04-01
cat 2020-04-07T{01..23}-00-00.log | grep 'getDepartureDetails' | jq -r .jsonPayload.request
```

<aside>
⚠️ Be careful when using `ls` into the root folder as there are a lot of files and it might take a while.

</aside>

> Wow! WTF is this last line?!
> 

Let’s explain the last line.

Remember, you are in a unix environnement so every unix tools are available. You can use `grep`, `cat`, `tail` or anything else.

In this example we first used `cat`, simply to display the content of our logs. Then, we piped `grep` to filter and only returned the request containing `getDepartureDetails` because we only want logs for those requests and finally we piped `jq` to output well formatted JSON.

Again, you can use all the tools you like if they are available in a unix environnement. Be creative and share your top commands with the team!

That’s all folks. Have fun playing with logs!

## The Doctor Report

When playing with integrations, an apple a day doesn’t keep the Doctor away BUT it’s a good thing because the Doctor is your friend.

`Doctor` is a command available in Flowbot giving you a full report on a specific route.

- Status of this route
- Number of departures available from partners
- Number of departures available on Busbud
- Number of departures not displayed on Busbud

So this is the perfect tool to debug if you can’t find a departure on Busbud when it should be there for example.

### How to use it

- Go on Slack
- Add Flowbot if it’s not already here and simply write:

```bash
doctor <link-from-busbud-to-inspect>
```

- Wait few seconds and you will get a link to the report

# How do I add a new payment <something>?

# How do I add a new payment… `<something>`?

The first thing to do is to identify what is it that you're looking to add.
Check out the [Glossary](../Glossary.md)  to understand the following concepts

- Payment provider
- Payment processor
- Payment gateway
- Payment method

In case the concepts are still a bit abstract, the following chart gives examples of each concept. Note that the graph contains a reduced set of information

```mermaid
flowchart
    subgraph Payment provider
    Adyen
    Spreedly
    MetroTurizm
    Stitch
    end
    subgraph Payment processor
    Adyen-->AdyenP[Adyen]
    Spreedly-->AdyenP[Adyen]
    Spreedly-->Ebanx
    Spreedly-->DLocal
    Spreedly-->MercadoPago
    Spreedly-->Moka
    MetroTurizm-->MetroTurizmP[MetroTurizm]
    Stitch-->StitchP[Stitch]
    end
    subgraph Payment gateway
    AdyenP-->BusbudAdyen,USD
    AdyenP-->BusbudAdyen,CAD
    AdyenP-->BusbudAdyen,EUR
    Ebanx-->BusbudEbanx,MXN
    Ebanx-->BusbudEbanx,PEN
    DLocal-->BusbudDLocal,ARS
    MercadoPago-->BusbudMercadoPago,ARS
    Moka-->BusbudMoka,TRY
    MetroTurizmP-->BusbudMetro,TRY
    StitchP-->BusbudStitch,ZAR
    end
    subgraph Payment method
    BusbudAdyen,USD-->GooglePay
    BusbudAdyen,USD-->ApplePay
    BusbudAdyen,USD-->Klarna
    BusbudAdyen,USD-->MBWay
    BusbudAdyen,USD-->CreditCard
    BusbudAdyen,CAD-->CreditCard
    BusbudAdyen,EUR-->CreditCard
    BusbudAdyen,EUR-->CreditCard
    BusbudEbanx,MXN-->CreditCard
    BusbudEbanx,PEN-->CreditCard
    BusbudDLocal,ARS-->CreditCard
    BusbudMercadoPago,ARS-->CreditCard
    BusbudMoka,TRY-->CreditCard
    BusbudMetro,TRY-->MetroTurizmWebsite
    BusbudStitch,ZAR-->StitchInstantPay
    end

```

Depending on what you're looking to add it is possible that you'll need to implement one or many of the concepts grouped above.
For example

1. Adding a direct integration such as stitch instant pay required us to introduce a payment provider, a gateway and payment method.
2. Changing our payment processor from DLocal to MercadoPago required us to only introduce the new payment processor and gateway.
3. Adding MBWay required us only to introduce an new payment method, because the rest already existed.

[Adding a New Payment Provider](../How Stuff Works/Payments and Purchases/Payment Providers.md) 

[Adding a New Payment Method](../How Stuff Works/Payments and Purchases/Payment Methods.md) 

[Adding a New Gateway](../How Stuff Works/Checkout/Gateways.md)

# How do I give access in Backoffice

# Overview

<aside>
🚨

If you have given access and the user can login but sees a subset of tabs, we might not have support for their domain. In that case reach out to platform-support channel to add new domains into the busbud permissions system.

</aside>

Below you can see snippets on how to give access or update it in backoffice, after following the steps a simple refresh should give the user access.

<aside>
🚨 Only reach out to rocket if you have followed the steps below and still are having issues. Sometimes it could be deactivated tokens or permissions + groups.

</aside>

## Give access

<aside>
💡

Remember we need an user created with that email on busbud.com

</aside>

1. Go to top right
2. Click on Admin
3. Use `access manager` tab
4. Enter the newly created users email
5. Add the permissions and click on `Give acccess`

See video: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_DKnXRMADLmm42zKR8N2MEvasuN_K_rT/view?t=4

## Update Existing User

1. Go to top right
2. Click on Admin
3. Use `token manager` tab
4. Enter the email of the user you want to update
5. Click `Search access`
6. Click on `Edit` for the token
7. Update any groups you want to give to the user

<aside>
💡 You can look at your other employees to mimic the groups needed by searching for the other employee, looking at the groups associated to them, then doing the same with the user you want to edit or update

If you run into issues, double check by viewing the permissions via the `edit` button. Then removing and adding the permissions again.

</aside>

See video: https://drive.google.com/file/d/11NYfSihzqhrd0sM9N-A-tcbp9RoUF55M/view?usp=drive_link

# Glossary

## Introduction

Language is important. We want to speak the same business language everywhere: in meetings, in documents, in code.

Here are the definitions of the specific concepts we talk about.

Also useful:

- [Adyen’s glossary](https://docs.adyen.com/get-started-with-adyen/payment-glossary)

## Payment provider

We call payment provider to the third party that allow us to accept payments.

From a technical perspective a payment provider corresponds to an implementation of the [PaymentProvider](https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/78647d8bac84083c9c6ec5422b81287d9b52ce5a/apps/bookie/components/payments/domain/model/payment-provider.ts#L13) interface.

<aside>
💡 *Hint: A payment provider is the equivalent to an “integration” in the supply world*

</aside>

<aside>
❓ [Learn more about this topic](/payments/how-it-works/payment-providers)

</aside>

## Payment processor

Refers to the party that process the payment. This could or not be the same as the payment provider.

For example: - Adyen is both a payment provider and a payment processor - Spreedly is a payment provider but they don’t process the payment. Instead they route the payment through different “gateways” that process the payment.

Is important to note that payment related inquiries should be directed to the payment processor and not the payment provider.

<aside>
💡 *Hint: A payment processor is the equivalent to a “source” in the supply world*

</aside>

## Payment method / Payment type

Payment method and payment type are used interchangeably. In the code you’ll mainly find “payment type” but “payment method” is preferred. It refers to the user facing payment method such as

- Card (debit or credit)
- Apple Pay
- Google Pay
- And many more.

Each payment provider supports a set of payment methods that may or may not be exclusive to them

## Gateway

A gateway in bookie (not to be confused with Spreedly’s gateway) is the combination of payment provider, payment processor and processing currency that we use to determine how customers will be charged. These configurations are defined in the `gateways` table which (simplified) looks like this

| Gateway | Payment provider | Payment processor | Currency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BusbudAdyen EUR | Adyen | Adyen | EUR |
| BusbudAdyen CAD | Adyen | Adyen | CAD |
| BusbudEbanx MXN | Spreedly | Ebanx | MXN |
| BusbudMercadoPago ARS | Spreedly | MercadoPago | ARS |

<aside>
❓ [Learn more about this topic](How Stuff Works/Checkout/Gateways.md)

</aside>

## Purchase

A purchase is completed after tickets are booked with the operator and payment has been processed. It consists of one or more ticket and can be completed on Busbud (BoB) or a partner’s website (BoX).

## Money

### Gross Merchandise Volume (GMV)

Also known as GBV or Gross Booking Value.

The money we receive in our bank account, before paying the operators and different costs. It’s equal to the amount the user paid for their tickets.

### Revenue

Money earned by Busbud for each ticket sale.

Can be represented as a flat rate (fixed amount per ticket/purchase), a percentage (fraction of the ticket value) or a markup (amount added to the ticket value).

### Net Revenue

Net revenues are equal to Gross revenues minus all Costs Of Goods Sold (COGS).

In our case, COGS include transaction processing fees and hosting costs. We do not really use that metric for the time being. It is called Gross Profit at many OTAs such as Expedia.

### Base Price

The price of a ticket without any taxes or fees (can be thought of as the supplier COGS).

### Markup

Amount added to the value of the ticket. Used in deals where we earn little to no percentage off the sale of the ticket.

### Supplier Fee

Fees added on top of the base price of a ticket by a supplier. This is represented separately in our infrastructure as our commission is usually a factor of the base price *excluding supplier fees*.

### Busbud Fee

Similar to markup, except is usually a flat fee (whereas markup is usually a percentage). These are often set per-source or per-region.

### Commission

It’s payed by the supplier, not the customer. It won’t be seen in the cart.

### FX

<aside>
❓ [Learn more about this topic](/payments/how-it-works/calculate-charges#money-conversion)

</aside>

Foreign Exchange. We use it to convert one currency into another. [See below](about:blank#currency) for when and why we convert currency.

## Fraud

<aside>
❓ [Learn more about this topic](/payments/how-it-works/fraud/)

</aside>

### Chargeback

When the credit card owner calls their bank to dispute the amount charged by Busbud, it is charged back to Busbud by the payment processor until the dispute is resolved.

### Fraud Risk Assessment Provider (FRAP)

A partner that’s responsible of determining if a transaction is fraudulent. E.g. Forter, Sift, Riskified, Konduto, etc. We currently use Forter as our FRAP.

### Friendly Fraud

When a legitimate user declares a fraud to get refunded for a non-refundable ticket. Frequent in markets like the US where most tickets are not refundable.

## Partners

### Agent

Operator/Supplier charges customer’s credit card and Busbud invoices operator/supplier to collect money.

Example: Busbud is a direct agent for Greyhound

### Merchant (of record)

Busbud charges customer’s credit card and operator/supplier invoices Busbud to collect money.

Example: Busbud is a direct merchant of record for Movelia

### Payment Method Distribution (PMD)

Special gateways associated with certain sources. It means that if we purchase with such a source, the gateway used will always be the one set in the source’s configuration (e.g. gateway_id). These sources process the user’s payment instead of us, so we encrypt and proxy their payment details to the supplier.

It’s called “PMD” because we kept Spreedly’s name.

There are several PMD sources. You can look them up in Grand Central’s DB with the following query:

```sql
SELECT * FROM sources WHERE gateway_id IS NOT NULL AND state = 'active';
```

As of Jan 2022, these are current PMD sources:

1. southeastern
2. sprinterbus
3. miller_hoosier
4. bestbus
5. metroturizm

### Operator

The bus company operating the departure.

### Supplier

Partner on the supply side (bus operator or aggregator). They “supply” us with the relevant data to provide search results for operators, and in the case of [BoB sources](about:blank#purchase), also allow us to complete bookings for those results.

### Distribution partner

Also known as demand partners. These are external organizations that consume our APIs with the goal of reselling our inventory on their sites.

### Referral partner

Referral partners are a specific kind of distribution partner. They set utm tags when deeplinking into busbud.com. They will redirect their users to the checkout page after they select their trip. If the trip is no longer available, then they fallback to results.

In bookie, we attribute sales made by these referral partners. You can look them up in bookie DB’s `purchase_attributions` table.

checkmybus is an example of a referral partner.

### Non-referral partner

Non-referral partners are the most common type of distribution partner. The largest non-referral partner we have is Trainline. They use both our search and booking APIs directly. Their `partner_id` is set in the purchases accordingly.

## Location

### Point of sale (PoSa)

Home country of the buyer. This is determined from the billing address / country provided by the user on the checkout page.

### Point of session (PoSe)

Country where buyer was located in when they completed their purchase (obtained from Google Analytics).

### Point of supply (PoSu)

Country of the departure city. This is how we think about markets (i.e. where we have inventory).

## Currency

### Source currency

Currency of the supplier of the bus ticket.

### Product currency

Currency of the cart item / ancillary product.

### User currency

Currency displayed to the user on the results page and on checkout. Also known as browsing currency.

### Processing currency

Currency in which we charge the user and process the payment, usually determined by the [PoSa](about:blank#point-of-sale-posa) combined with currencies in which we offer local processing. Example: if a user’s PoSa is South Africa, we will charge them in ZAR as we offer local processing in this currency.

When the processing currency differs from the user currency, we provide the actual processing currency and amount on the checkout page so the user knows what to expect.

Exceptions to how we determine processing currency:

- In Argentina, due to local regulations, we charge users in ARS when the source currency is also ARS, but in USD in every other case.

### Settlement currency

Currency of the money we receive in our bank account from the payment processor.

# Add new Currency

When a new source requires a new currency, we must ensure our services support this currency. We also need to wait for approval from the finance team, as they need to check whether we can pay the partner in that currency.

- [ ]  Get Finance approval for new source
- [ ]  Update the prices package (see https://github.com/busbud/napi/pull/11137/files)
    - [ ]  Update package version: https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/0bc2c4d73c59936e14cb611a3efa5197b7ab5a4f/packages/prices/package.json#L3
    - [ ]  Add currency on the types: https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/0bc2c4d73c59936e14cb611a3efa5197b7ab5a4f/packages/prices/src/types/common.ts#L3
- [ ]  Update Grand-Central:
    - [ ]  Bump `@busbud/prices` packages: https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/0bc2c4d73c59936e14cb611a3efa5197b7ab5a4f/apps/grand-central/package.json#L18
    - [ ]  Add new currency on `supported_source_currencies` https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/73561def1617362d398e44ca81ddd64849081a02/apps/grand-central/routes/sources.js#L27
    - [ ]  Refresh the exchange rates default config and ensure the new currency is included: https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/73561def1617362d398e44ca81ddd64849081a02/apps/grand-central/config/exchange-rates.js#L125
    - [ ]  Search Grand-Central’s code to ensure there aren’t any new places with currencies
- [ ]  Update Bookie’s (see https://github.com/busbud/napi/pull/11101 as a basis)
    - [ ]  Bump `@busbud/prices` packages: https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/0bc2c4d73c59936e14cb611a3efa5197b7ab5a4f/apps/bookie/package.json#L137
    - [ ]  Add currency config: https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/73561def1617362d398e44ca81ddd64849081a02/apps/bookie/config/currencies.ts#L277
    - [ ]  Add currency on exchange-rate DB model: https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/73561def1617362d398e44ca81ddd64849081a02/apps/bookie/models/db/exchange-rates.ts#L109
    - [ ]  Add currency on fx function to refresh from cache: https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/73561def1617362d398e44ca81ddd64849081a02/apps/bookie/lib/fx.js#L84
    - [ ]  Add currency on list of supported currencies: https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/73561def1617362d398e44ca81ddd64849081a02/apps/bookie/packages/bookie/src/core/currency.ts#L32
    - [ ]  Create new migration to add the currency on the exchange rates table (similar to https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/73561def1617362d398e44ca81ddd64849081a02/apps/bookie/migrations/20230720142222-add-ngn.js#L6)
    - [ ]  Search Bookie’s code to ensure there aren’t any new places with currencies
- [ ]  Update Backoffice
    - [ ]  Add the new currency as a currency option for dropdowns: https://github.com/busbud/frontier/blob/04373a9f9be131b44ff171f50e55cc90fc56a6cd/apps/backoffice/src/pages/dashboard/common/utils/select-options.ts#L1
    - [ ]  Add it as a currency constant: https://github.com/busbud/frontier/blob/04373a9f9be131b44ff171f50e55cc90fc56a6cd/apps/backoffice/src/pages/shared/core/constants/Constants.ts#L968
    - [ ]  Search Frontier’s code to ensure there aren’t any new places with currencies
- [ ]  Update `dolla-bills`:
    - [ ]  Add it on the require currencies array: https://github.com/busbud/dolla-bills/blob/0d249ad784bba8ef12c13c3e32914d832a87a125/refresh.js#L17
    - [ ]  Add it on the test as well: https://github.com/busbud/dolla-bills/blob/0d249ad784bba8ef12c13c3e32914d832a87a125/refresh.spec.js#L23
    - [ ]  Search `dolla-bills`’ code to ensure there aren’t any new places with currencies

# Add new Passenger Question

From time to time we need to add a new passenger question. This requires updates in a few different places:

- [ ]  Add a new question Integration Packages:
    - [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/integration-packages/blob/master/packages/integration-schemas/lib/questions.ts
- [ ]  Add translations for the question Key on bookie:
    - [ ]  Example PR: https://github.com/busbud/napi/pull/12061/files

# How to launch new Betterez Supply

Note: this page is only for those authorized to use the service. If you aren’t part of the supply squad engineering team, nor its PM, please don’t use it.

# Overview

Link to backoffice: [https://backoffice.busbud-int.com/dashboard/ims/betterez-sources/new](https://backoffice.busbud-int.com/dashboard/ims/betterez-sources/new)

We have a tool that helps us automate adding new betterez sources and completes most of the flow. This page is meant to be a guide on how to fill out the form, where to get its values, and a walkthrough of the few last steps before the supply can go live.

# 1. Creating a New Job for the Betterez Service

There’s two flows to the Betterez service, one for a regular Betterez integration (Busbud sells supply via Betterez), and an extra one where we also make the whitelabel for the supplier. The latter is an add-on of the former. 

Note that all information should be available on the new source’s github issue before a job should be created. From project management perspective, if the GitHub issue does not have all the information required, or the information is malformed, then it is not ready for the Supply Squad to look at.

## Creating a Betterez Automated Job for new Busbud Supply

To create a new Betterez source, we have to fill out the following form:

![image.png](How%20to%20launch%20new%20Betterez%20Supply/image.png)

The answer to most of these questions should be readily available within the Github Issue. The text below describes in more detail of what each field is expecting

### Source Name

This is the source name that will be the unique identifier for the source in our database. It cannot be changed after creation, and only uses a combination of lowercase letters and underscores (`_`). This field is not shown to any external people, only used as our internal identifier when communicating internally.

For example:

- a company called `Ontario Northland` is called `ontarionorthland` as the source name
- a company called `Movelia` is called `moveliaudm` in our systems because of some internal reasons, even though `udm` means nothing to Movelia

For Betterez sources, typically the source name is just the lowercase name of the company, without any spaces. It should also be already given at the very top of the Github Issue.

### Display Name

This is the actual name of the company to be displayed to our users. It should be properly capitalized and punctuated as the supplier prefers

### Adapter Deployment

This is a technical field, that has to do with how the betterez integration is set up. We try to mitigate risk such that in the case of complete failure of one supplier, only the deployment of that one supplier will break down.

In essence:

- If the operator is a small business in LATAM (Latin America), choose `LATAM`
- If the operator is a small shuttle service (few routes, or just has a vehicle type of “shuttle”), choose `shuttle`
- Otherwise just use the default
- You will never need to use `Ontario Northland` nor `Pacific Western`

### Currency

This is the currency the supplier will deal with. It should be given in the Github Issue.

### Source Display URL

This is the URL of the supplier’s **own** website. 

For example:

- for `Ontario Northland` it is `www.ontarionorthland.ca`

Remove any `https://` in the url for this field.

### Notification Emails

Sometimes the Betterez supplier does not have a good mechanism to see their new purchases.  If this is the case, the GitHub issue will mention a notification email that they want to set.

If not given, you can assume there’s none, and leave this field empty.

We can also easily add one after all is said and done, so no stress.

### Betterez Provider/Account ID

This is a field given by Betterez. It should already exist on the Github issue. This is the ID of the supplier’s Betterez account. Without it, we **definitely cannot continue**.

### Payment Method

This is a technical field also specified by Betterez. It is very rare that it is specified. When it isn’t mentioned, you can leave it blank.

### Vehicle Type

This is the type of vehicle that the company runs. It should be given in the GitHub issue.

### QR Code Message Prefix

This is a long story, but we’re essentially looking for the prefix of the supplier’s *betterez* URL. Betterez should supply this on setup.

For example:

- Ontario Northland has a betterez URL of `ontarionorthland.betterez.com` . Therefore, the answer to this field is `ontarionorthland`
- Pacific Western has a betterez URL of `pwt.betterez.com`. Therefore, the answer to this field is `pwt`

If Betterez is not supplying this info, you can to try and find this yourself, by testing some educated guesses on the url. If you get the betterez user login screen, you’ve hit the jackpot.

### Done

If you do not have to create a whitelabel, you can hit the `Create` button on the top right of the screen, and move on to reading the job status.

## Creating a whitelabel for the supplier

To further create a whitelabel for the supplier, you can hit the `Create Whitelabel` toggle, which will open up a few extra fields. The answers to these fields should be found on the `ecommerce` tab of the Busbud Checklist. If they’re not filled, then the entire task - including the source creation - is blocked.

![image.png](How%20to%20launch%20new%20Betterez%20Supply/image%201.png)

### Subdomain Preview and Root Preview

First read and complete `Subdomain Production and Root Production`.

The preview equivalents aren’t typically given in the checklist because no one really looks at preview except engineers. You can leave `root preview` to be equivalent to `root production`, and append the Subdomain Production value with `-preview` for `subdomain preview`.

For example:

- for a `Subdomain Production` of `ontarionorthland`, your `Subdomain Preview` will be `ontarionorthland-preview`

### Subdomain Production and Root Production

These two fields define what the partner wants their URL to be. These should be given in the checklist under `What domain do you want for the E-Commerce site?` and `What name should be shown in the E-Commerce URL? Tip: Keep it short and easy to type.` 

The domain answer in the checklist is the answer to `Root Production` while the answer to the name is the `Subdomain Production`. The combination of these two answers should be the final URL for the partner’s whitelabel.

For example:

- A domain of `<operator>.vehicle-tickets.com` and a name of `ontarionorthland` will result in the following field answers:
    - Subdomain production: `ontarionorthland`
    - Root Production: `.vehicle-tickets.com`
    
    Which results in a final URL of `ontarionorthland.vehicle-tickets.com`
    

### Whitelabel Theme

This is the color theme the partner would like for their whitelabel. It should be specified in the checklist under `what theme color do you want for your ecommerce?` The answer should be one of the 12 colors.

### Whitelabel Preset

Select `default`.

### Logo

Upload the logo that the operator has provided you. Do not try to find one on the internet because we’ve previously run into problems where they’ve complained about the quality, or that the logo is old. Always use the one given to you on the checklist.

### Done

When the entire form is filled out, click `Create`!

## Reading the Job

After creating the job, you should be redirected to a page that views the current status of the job. You can also view it any time in backoffice under the tab `IMS Integrations` -> `Jobs` and clicking on the one you created.

TODO: add screenshot of backoffice page

In a job, the automation is doing a list of actions in the background, and you can view this pipeline on the page. If a step in the pipeline fails, the job will safely roll itself back, to return everything to the state is was in before the job started. Below will go through each step and what to do when it fails.

### Create Job

This is just the step that creates the job on the service to keep track of its progress. It will rarely fail. If it fails, the betterez service must be down entirely, and an engineer on the Supply Squad should be notified (whoever is on helpdesk rotation that week)

### Preflight Check On Integration

In this step, we run the credentials given in the form against the Betterez API to make sure it works. There’s a number of API calls that must return information from the Betterez API, or else we won’t receive results.

A number of failure messages can occur:

- `No Busbud account found for the currency <currency>. Please reach out to #betterez-busbud-support2 for one.`
    - This means we don’t have a betterez account in the selected currency yet. Like the message suggests, you can reach out the the betterez team in the #betterez-busbud-support2 channel to get one. Once we have an account, the Supply Squad can easily add it on our side in a few minutes.
- `There are no products exposed to Busbud via the Betterez API`
    - This means the API is not returning any Betterez products. You can reach out to the betterez team at #betterez-busbud-support2 with your providerID and say “there’s no products for this providerID”
- `There are no fares exposed to Busbud via the Betterez API`
    - same idea as products, except now you’re dealing with fares. Same solution, reach out to the betterez team at #betterez-busbud-support2 with your providerID and say “there’s no fares for this providerID”
- `There are no locations/stations exposed to Busbud via the Betterez API`
    - same idea as products and fares. same solution.
- `Error Request to Betterez failed`
    - This is a generic error message that can mean anything BUT in our case it almost always is that Betterez hasn’t given our account the correct access. Before looping in an engineer, it will always be worth asking on #betterez-busbud-support2 channel “Can you check our access for OPERATOR (provider_id: <providerID>) for our <currency> account”?
        - For example: “can you check our access for OntarioNorthland (providerID: 52f862392433e2310400004d) for our CAD account”
    - If the following doesn’t work, you can loop in a Supply Squad engineer, who can most-likely diagnose very fast.

Once the preflight check completes, it’ll keep an informational field on the fare names given by the supplier. This is important because we need to map this to a proper fare on our side. Typically if the names are just `adult`, `child`, `standard` etc, which are all fine and already accounted for. If you run into a really unique fare name such as `BUSBUD ONLY NEVER SEEN BEFORE FARE NAME` , it’ll need to be added to our [master list](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/master/betterezudm/src/adapter/domain/fares/default.ts#L34) before searches will return results.

### TODO

The rest of the steps

# 2. Populating Backoffice

Once your automated Betterez job is completed, our next goal is to trigger a successful search, that will populate backoffice with all the data we need before launch.

**Note: there are a LOT of things that can go wrong here, if something isn’t working, feel free to reach out to the Supply Lead (at time of writing, Lisa), who can unblock and tell you what’s wrong in about 3 seconds flat**

## You will need

- Backoffice:
    - XMappings access: https://backoffice.busbud-int.com/dashboard/x-mappings
    - Sources access: https://backoffice.busbud-int.com/dashboard/bus-company/sources
    - Operators access: https://backoffice.busbud-int.com/dashboard/bus-company/operators
- The Busbud Chrome extension: [https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/busbud-extension/igjgmjmlniaagjlooahnibmhangcilld](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/busbud-extension/igjgmjmlniaagjlooahnibmhangcilld)
- A Busbud account with your Terra email
    - Go on [busbud.com](http://busbud.com) and sign in with Google if you haven’t already

## Find XMappings for the source

On backoffice, go [here](https://backoffice.busbud-int.com/dashboard/x-mappings) or from the homepage `Geo Data -> X-Mappings`  and search for the new source name you created: 

![image.png](How%20to%20launch%20new%20Betterez%20Supply/image%202.png)

![image.png](How%20to%20launch%20new%20Betterez%20Supply/image%203.png)

If you can’t find it, make sure your Betterez job in step (1) actually completed. Most likely, it didn’t succeed.

After hitting the Magnifying Glass to search, you’ll be greeted with our Xmappings interface:

![image.png](How%20to%20launch%20new%20Betterez%20Supply/image%204.png)

The important parts here are the `Operator XIDs` and `Mapped` columns.

❗🎉 If you already see values in the `Operator Xids` field, you can skip straight to the section [Creating the Slack Message](How to launch new Betterez Supply.md) 

Our goal for this section is to make sure at least **two** XMappings have a green checkmark in the `Mapped` column, like the three XMappings do in the screenshot above. 

❗🎉 If you already have two XMappings with a green checkmark, you can skip straight to the section [Refreshing the Routes](How to launch new Betterez Supply.md) 

If that is not the case, then you can enlist some help from Supply QA via the `#supply-qa` slack channel:

- Fill out their slack workflow by clicking on this button:

![image.png](How%20to%20launch%20new%20Betterez%20Supply/image%205.png)

- and filling out the form like this:

![image.png](How%20to%20launch%20new%20Betterez%20Supply/image%206.png)

- for inputs:
    - Request category will be `Supply Missing`
    - Priority is low
    - Operator Name/ Source Name is the source name you gave your new source (ie `jasperlimousine`)
    - Busbud/Doctor link is a link to backoffice’s xmappings view for jasperlimousine
    - In `what's wrong`, put a little bit of context about the ask itself. You can copy and paste below
    
    ```
    Need some help with a new incoming source called <Insert Source Name>. 
    Can you help me map a couple of its xmappings so I can perform some test searches?
    Please and thank you!
    ```
    

## Refreshing the Routes

After supplyQA is done, we need to sync up a bunch of databases in order to perform the search. To do this, on any page in Backoffice, hit the `Refresh Routes` button on the top-right corner of your screen: 

![image.png](How%20to%20launch%20new%20Betterez%20Supply/image%207.png)

After, go for a very long coffee break ☕☕☕☕☕☕☕

Even better, to maximize success, come back tomorrow.

## Performing a search

Now we are ready to try and perform a search on Busbud.com.

Requirements:

- Make sure you are logged in with your Busbud email
- Open your Busbud Chrome Extension, scroll to the very bottom of `Feature Flags` which has a field called `search-source-state`

![image.png](How%20to%20launch%20new%20Betterez%20Supply/image%208.png)

- Set the `search-source-state` to `active, darklaunch` or just `darklaunch` (either works)

![image.png](How%20to%20launch%20new%20Betterez%20Supply/image%209.png)

Now we need a route to perform a search on. For this, we go back to the XMappings view on Backoffice and filter by `Mapped = true`, these are the possible locations we can search for. Select two of them that hopefully have inventory between them. You can figure out which cities they are by clicking on each of them and you’ll see a Location → City field on the right half of the page 

![image.png](How%20to%20launch%20new%20Betterez%20Supply/image%2010.png)

After getting the two cities, you can fill them in the Busbud search bar and hit search!:

![image.png](How%20to%20launch%20new%20Betterez%20Supply/image%2011.png)

⚠️ Note: you will not see any results. This is completely normal ⚠️

For good measure, search a few extra dates as well, and maybe also the opposite route (switch origin and destinations).

Now, if we refresh the Backoffice XMappings page, hopefully the `Operator Xids` is populated for AT LEAST one xmapping (you don’t need all)

![image.png](How%20to%20launch%20new%20Betterez%20Supply/image%2012.png)

If not, call Lisa.

## Creating the Slack Message

You are now ready to create a new message on the slack `new-supply-onboarding` channel.

Select the `New Supply Via Betterez` workflow

![image.png](How%20to%20launch%20new%20Betterez%20Supply/image%2013.png)

and fill out its contents:

- Supply Region: the part of the world the supply operates in
- Partnerships Manager: typically, this is just the person who created the Github Issue. It is the business team member that signed the deal.
- Finance Manager: this is prefilled with Mary, but if the deal is in Mexico or LATAM, click the field to select `@latambusops` instead
- Supplier display name: the official name of the supplier. with capitalization and all. Same as the `Display Name` when filling out the betterez job. In the example above, this would be `Jasper Limousine`
- Busbud source name: the name of the source on busbud to search with. In the example above, this would be `jasperlimousine`
- Busbud source ID: this is the numerical ID for the source on Busbud. You can find it in many places, but for convenience, here’s the two popular ones:
    - If you still have your Betterez job open, the completed job will have the ID at the top (3287 in this example):
    
    ![image.png](How%20to%20launch%20new%20Betterez%20Supply/image%2014.png)
    
    - If not, you can get it by going on backoffice `Inventory -> Sources` then search for your source name. The header will give you the Source ID:

![image.png](How%20to%20launch%20new%20Betterez%20Supply/image%2015.png)

- Betterez Provider ID: this is again the providerID that should be available in your Github issue
- Betterez Version: This can be answered via the `type` in the Github issue. Most commonly, it’ll be `Regular`
- Currency: also available in the Github issue.
- Cancellation type:
    - If the `betterez version` is regular, then the answer here is `API Self-Serve`
    - if the `betterez version` is no excuses, then the answer here is `operator Contact`
- What needs to be mapped: check off the following:
    - Operator: always
    - T&Cs: always
    - Classes: always
    - Xmappings (were automapped): only if all the XMappings have a green checkmark in the `mapped` column
    - Xmappings (need some help after the automapper): if the above one wasn’t checked off
- Test Route: you can give the route you used in [Performing a search](How to launch new Betterez Supply.md), OR in the Github issue, there should be listed trophy routes
- Link to Onboarding Checklist: copy the link of the checklist in the github issue
- Notes: you typically won’t need.

After you send this off, multiple teams will be tagged via automation, as they all have a part to do. There is generally nothing else for you to do, until the partnerships manager asks if everyone is ready, in which case, you can say “ready!”

## Go-Live

Partnerships Manager is in charge of officially turning on the supply. Once it has been turned on, we can mark the Github issue as completed.

# Update Partner ID

Finance considers Demand Partners and Sources as Vendors; and therefore they are stored on the same table on Netsuite and cannot have conflicting IDs.

Due to this limitation, we updated partners to use different IDs to prevent conflicts, so today Partners have IDs starting at 100xxx, and Sources have IDs starting at 3xxx.

But, from time to time we see conflicting cases based on previous partners/sources from before the change, and it requires us to manually update the PK on the Partner table (a really good example of an anti-pattern IMO, but, it seems we cannot change the behaviour on Netsuite ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ ).

This checklist should cover all tables and places where we should take a look at before updating the ID on the Partner table.

For both `prod` and `preview`:

- Check Grand Central's DB:
    - [ ]  Update `partners` table on GC prod
    - [ ]  Check if we need to update `partner_compensation_rules`, and if so update it
    - [ ]  Check if we need to update `partners_sources` , and if so update it
    - [ ]  Check every supply rule and update the `partner_id` where necessary
    
    ```sql
    -- Example query to help:
    SELECT *
    FROM supply_rules
    WHERE 
    	triggers::TEXT like '%"307"%' 
    	OR criterias::TEXT like '%"307"%';
    ```
    

- Check Bookie's DB:
    - [ ]  Check if we need to update `purchases`, and if so update it
- Check Il-Controllore’s DB:
    - [ ]  Check if we need to update `tokens`, and if so update it

# Update Terms Checklist

Terms & Conditions displayed on `pubweb` and mobile apps are JSON objects that must follow a specific JSON schema. They are created/updated on Backoffice, stored in Grand-Central and rendered into human readable mobile or web T&Cs by `busbud-terms`. Their typescript interfaces are stored in `core-types` and used by `poll-service` and `pubweb`.

This means that updating the schemas requires us to update multiple repositories. The checklist below includes a list of all repositories that requires changes when updating T&Cs schemas:

# Checklist

- [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/busbud-schemas - update JSON schemas (only used by Grand-Central)
- [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/busbud-terms
    - [ ]  Update how T&Cs are rendered on `packages/busbud-terms`  (translations may be required)
    - [ ]  Link to local public-website, to ensure the new terms are being displayed as intended. If not, you might have to come back here for future fixes
    - [ ]  Ping mobile squads (after the docs are updated) so they can update the mobile packages
- [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/integration-packages
    - [ ]  Update `core-types` TypeScript interfaces
    - [ ]  Add new values to `core-factories`
- [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/poll-service
    - [ ]  Bump `core-types` , `core-factories`
    - [ ]  Fix all build errors and double check any T&Cs models
- [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/frontier
    - [ ]  Bump `core-types`
    - [ ]  Make sure the new schema values for T&Cs can be updated
    - [ ]  Note: the “preview” button on T&Cs links to pubweb, which is the next step below
- [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/public-website
    - [ ]  bump `core-types` and `busbud-terms` , fix build errors
    - [ ]  Some tests may also need to be updated
    - [ ]  Link to local backoffice to check if the preview displays as needed
- [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/napi/
    - [ ]  bump `busbud-schemas`
    - [ ]  `apps/grand-central/routes/helpers/terms-helpers.js` may need to be updated
- [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/frontier/ - Update `Backoffice` to properly generate new/updated terms
- [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/docs - Update documentation
- [ ]  Other repositories to bump up https://github.com/busbud/busbud-terms
    - [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/il-postino
    - [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/autoresponder
    - [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/hodor
    - [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/busbud-support
- [ ]  If any fields are deprecated in favour of others, run scripts to migrate the data

## Markdown

You can copy this markdown on the Github issue to help track progress:

```markdown
- [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/busbud-schemas - update JSON schemas (only used by Grand-Central)
- [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/busbud-terms
    - [ ]  Update how T&Cs are rendered on `packages/busbud-terms` (translations may be required)
    - [ ]  Ping mobile squads so they can update the mobile packages
- [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/integration-packages
    - [ ]  Update `core-types` TypeScript interfaces
- [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/poll-service
    - [ ]  Bump `core-types`
    - [ ]  Fix all build errors and double check any T&Cs models
- [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/public-website
    - [ ]  bump `core-types` and `busbud-terms`
    - [ ]  Some tests may also need to be updated
- [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/napi/
    - [ ]  bump `busbud-schemas`
    - [ ]  `apps/grand-central/routes/helpers/terms-helpers.js` may need to be updated
- [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/frontier/ - Update `Backoffice` to properly generate new/updated terms
- [ ]  https://github.com/busbud/docs - Update documentation
- [ ]  Other repositories to bump up `busbud-terms`
    - [ ] https://github.com/busbud/il-postino
    - [ ] https://github.com/busbud/autoresponder
    - [ ] https://github.com/busbud/hodor
    - [ ] https://github.com/busbud/busbud-support
- [ ] If any fields are deprecated in favour of others, run scripts to migrate the data
```

# Example

Recent example of T&Cs updates PRs:

- https://github.com/busbud/busbud-schemas: https://github.com/busbud/busbud-schemas/pull/107
- https://github.com/busbud/busbud-terms: https://github.com/busbud/busbud-terms/pull/229
- https://github.com/busbud/integration-packages: https://github.com/busbud/integration-packages/pull/1266
- https://github.com/busbud/poll-service: https://github.com/busbud/poll-service/pull/1510
- https://github.com/busbud/public-website: https://github.com/busbud/public-website/pull/22138
- https://github.com/busbud/napi/: https://github.com/busbud/napi/pull/12211
- https://github.com/busbud/frontier/: https://github.com/busbud/frontier/pull/324
- https://github.com/busbud/docs: https://github.com/busbud/docs/pull/507

# Cart

# Overview

At a high-level, here are the required calls a client has to do to create and purchase a Cart on Bookie:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User 👤
    participant C as Client
    participant B as Bookie

    U->>C:Select trip
    C->>B:POST /carts
    B-->>C:Created cart 🛒
```

## Context

Busbud has two main payment integrations on the consumer-facing side: Spreedly and Adyen.

Payment Gateway configuration is largely contained within Bookie’s `gateways` database table.

If paying with credit cards, we must know which form to display based on the context (currency) and stick to it throughout the purchase process. This implies making the most appropriate Gateway selection early on and sticking to that choice (unless the currency changes).

We want to optimize the choice of the billing currency to lower transaction processing costs.

## How we create the Cart

Let’s walk through the part relating to platform (spreedly/adyen) selection, using Pubweb and legacy cart API version:

1. Pubweb provides [the payment platforms it supports](https://github.com/busbud/public-website/blob/8e6d0f6b52c9db17c876fc87674dc00baba93735/app/services/api.ts#L252) in the `Create Cart` call.
2. On Bookie, [the `CartInfo` is created](https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/bf829e405fb72953cf76416fb583f4032f51250f/apps/bookie/components/cart/application/service/build-cart.ts#L24)
3. The Cart [is saved to redis](https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/bf829e405fb72953cf76416fb583f4032f51250f/apps/bookie/components/cart/infrastructure/repository/redis-cart-repository.ts#L93)
4. [We prepare the data](https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/bf829e405fb72953cf76416fb583f4032f51250f/apps/bookie/routes/cart/v1/commons/response.ts#L94) for the response that will represent the Cart (`buildCartContextForResponse`). Note that all the steps that follow right below are part of this [function](https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/bf829e405fb72953cf76416fb583f4032f51250f/apps/bookie/components/cart/related-models.ts#L25).
5. [Payment types](https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/bf829e405fb72953cf76416fb583f4032f51250f/apps/bookie/components/cart/related-models.ts#L346), such as credit Card, Apple Pay, etc…, are set on the Cart, depending on their config toggles.
    1. In Adyen’s case, we must communicate to them the context (e.g. currency, country code and locale) in order for them to tell us which payment types are available per merchant account, which is done [here](https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/bf829e405fb72953cf76416fb583f4032f51250f/apps/bookie/components/cart/application/service/get-adyen-payment-methods.ts#L37). But, the call to Adyen’s [`/paymentMethods`](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/CheckoutService/v67/post/paymentMethods) endpoint happens after we call `loadPaymentTypes` function.
    2. In the cases of a partner’s calls, they have [supported payment types config](https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/bf829e405fb72953cf76416fb583f4032f51250f/apps/bookie/components/cart/related-models.ts#L369-L371).
    3. There is the case of Spreedly PMD payments where [a source has a very specific Gateway configured that we must use](https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/bf829e405fb72953cf76416fb583f4032f51250f/apps/bookie/components/cart/related-models.ts#L67-L69). This forces usage of Spreedly, and of that specific gateway, throughout the process.
6. [The payment platform](https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/bf829e405fb72953cf76416fb583f4032f51250f/apps/bookie/components/cart/related-models.ts#L202) (Spreedly vs Adyen mainly) selection is made based on the following criteria. It is saved on the `payment_platforms` attribute of the Cart and will be part of the response. This choice helps with the actual Gateway selection of the next step:
    1. Is `ADYEN_ENABLED` true? (Spreedly integration has no such toggle)
    2. What were the platforms provided at Step 1? (client supported platforms)
    3. Which platform is appropriate for the given user currency?
    4. At Cart Creation, the payment type defaults to credit card.
    5. This looks at the `gateways` database table to search within active gateways.
    6. If nothing is found, an attempt is made with the fallback currency of USD.
7. [The appropriate gateway](https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/bf829e405fb72953cf76416fb583f4032f51250f/apps/bookie/components/cart/related-models.ts#L56) entry (from the database) is selected based on the platform selected in the last step and the user currency. The selection will also be affected by the billing country and gateway restrictions (more on that later).
    1. In the rare edge case of the Spreedly PMD Fake Roundtrip scenario, you may have [two segments with different gateways](https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/bf829e405fb72953cf76416fb583f4032f51250f/apps/bookie/components/cart/domain/model/trip.ts#L102-L109). One of the gateways would be forced by the source, and the other is forced by a gateway where Busbud processes the payment.
    2. Next section will dig deeper in Gateway.findByCurrency() and the possible scenarios around it.
8. [A list of Supported Credit Card types](https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/bf829e405fb72953cf76416fb583f4032f51250f/apps/bookie/components/cart/related-models.ts#L106) are added as an attribute to the Cart when the credit-card payment type is selected. This list is used by Pubweb for 1) icon display and 2) credit card number format validation against known card type formats. The values come from a Bookie database table `supported_credit_cards` with a direct foreign key link to the `gateways` table.
    1. Complexity comes from having multiple platforms and the historical (and now still existing but rare) possibility of having to consider multiple gateways and how they might support different types of cards (PMD scenario).
9. A list of available payment methods, based on the user’s context (user_id, currency, $ amount), is retrieved from the Adyen integration (maps to [Adyen’s `/paymentMethods`](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/CheckoutService/v67/post/paymentMethods)).
    1. The results of this call are cached into the same cache where the carts are stored in Redis. We had performance issues before doing the caching since this was too frequently called.
    2. In an ideal world, this call would happen at the moment where after “we are done” calculating the cart’s charges (the user made all his choices) and right before presenting payment options (the user is ready to pay). Current cart implementations and UX flows are too coupled with payments to make this possible, therefore the call happens at this moment.
10. [A JSON payload is built out](https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/bf829e405fb72953cf76416fb583f4032f51250f/apps/bookie/routes/cart/v1/commons/response.ts#L109) of all the data recovered from the last steps and sent out as a response to Pubweb.
11. Pubweb then [knows how to render the appropriate payment form](https://github.com/busbud/public-website/blob/e24603c0b2e792c530085ad81073b3eb265650ca/app/modules/checkout/components/payment-section/payment-form/payment-form.tsx#L183) based on the Cart response.

## How the Cart can be modified

The Cart has been created as described above. Great!

However, with the current implementation, we allow users to change the currency, which has an impact on the availability of payment methods and the gateway selection.

### Currency Change

[A currency change by the user](https://github.com/busbud/public-website/blob/e24603c0b2e792c530085ad81073b3eb265650ca/app/modules/checkout/components/price-information/currency-selector.tsx#L27) will trigger [a fresh fetching of the Cart](https://github.com/busbud/public-website/blob/e24603c0b2e792c530085ad81073b3eb265650ca/app/modules/checkout/actions/update-currency.js#L35), with the new currency as a parameter. All the steps (4 to 11) described above about building out the data for the Cart JSON response will run again, resulting in:

- Re-calculation of the Cart Charges
- A fresh call to Adyen’s GET /paymentMethods.
    - ApplePay and GooglePay and other payment methods are not available for all the same currencies as credit card payments.
- Possibility of a new gateway being selected by Bookie and assigned to the Cart
- Possibility of Pubweb rendering a UI if the gateway changes

These last two points are likely on the passenger step of checkout.

Imagine the scenario of switching from `CAD`, where the Adyen form is used, to a currency like `MXN` where only the Spreedly form may be used. On the passenger step, you’d go from having the option to choose between Google Pay or credit card to having credit card as the only payment option because we don’t offer Google Pay with Spreedly.

On the payment step, you’re very much likely not going to see a new gateway being selected because it is primarily determined by billing country, not user currency. If a currency is changed, then the user would be seeing the prices in the new currency, which would not match the processing currency.

A really good way to see this in action is to go on Busbud Preview and create a Cart while browsing in `EUR`, `CAD` or `USD`, and once you land on the passenger section, change the currency to `MXN`.

### Billing Country Change

We want to optimize the choice of the billing currency to lower transaction processing costs. For credit card payments, this generally means billing people in the currency of the country where their credit card originates from.

This means that you should be able to see in action something similar to the manual currency change whenever you input a Country in the Billing Address country field.

For example, if you were browsing in `EUR` but you then select `Canada` as the billing country, the billing currency will change to `CAD`, and you will see this:

# Instalments

Instalments tend to work differently by country, and especially so by payment provider.

## How it works

Instalments as a payment method are only available for gateways that support it. You can look them up with this query:

```sql
select * from gateways where installments_supported is true;
```

The following conditions must be met in order for instalments to be offered to the users:

- `installments_supported` is true for a gateway
- The user currency and the gateway's currency (aka billed currency) are the same

Here's a walkthrough of how it's done with legacy API:

- For some of the cart's endpoints, the `installments_plan` is defined in one of the middlewares. The client may provide the instalment plans in the payload. If it is not provided, then we default to an empty instalment plan, which is treated as a regular payment:

```jsx
// Empty installment plan
{
  id: null,
  installments: 1,
  installment_amount: null,
  total_amount: null
}

// Installment plan
{
  id: null,
  installments: 3,
  installment_amount: 10,
  total_amount: 30
}
```

- We have two ways of handling instalments: internal and external.

### Internal

We call it internal if we choose the interest rate and decide on a set of number of instalments for the user to pay in. For example, we can offer to the users an option to pay in either 1, 2, 3, 6, or 12 instalments for the Mexican gateway.

- If the user opts not to pay in instalments, then we do nothing. The `calculateCharges` function will return the charges as it is.
- If the user opts to pay in instalments (`installments` > 1), then the calculateCharges function will update cart charges to include the interest in the total amount.

There are two different types of interest rate: simple (one-time interest rate) and monthly interest rate.

### External

We call it external when we don't decide on the instalment plans to offer to the users. dLocal gateway is the only one that uses this use case.

- The clients make a HTTP POST request to `/installments-plans`. This is usually done at checkout when the users is providing their card info in the payment form.
- The backend fetches the available instalment plans from an external API (e.g. dLocal)
- If the user opts to pay in instalments, then the client fetches the cart with HTTP GET request to `/cart/:cart_id`, providing the selected instalment plan in the query payload.
- On the backend, we update the instalment plan in the middleware.
- We pass the instalment plan to `calculateCharges` method, where the cart charges will be updated.

In both cases, the `calculateCharges` method will include the instalment plans (including interest rate/amount, type of interest rate) in the response so that the payment details are transparent to the users (e.g. how much is the interest?).

**Example**

Given a trip of 10$ and an instalment plan with interest rate of 20%

If the plan is an internal one

- We display the total charges to the user: 10$ subtotal + 2$ interest
- We charge the customer 12$, the gateway will divide those 12$ monthly

If the plan is a external one

- We display the total charges to the user: 10$ subtotal + 2$ interest
- We charge the customer 10$, the gateway will apply the 2$ interest on top of that and split the payment monthly

## Brazil (Adyen)

For Brazil, we use the instalments functionality provided by our [Adyen integration](https://docs.adyen.com/payment-methods/installment-payments).

On the engineering side, it is rather simple. The payload to the call to Adyen’s /payments must simply include [the number of instalments](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/PaymentSetupAndVerificationService/v51/payments__reqParam_installments), and we can bump the dollar amount sent to Adyen to include interests that will end up in Busbud’s pockets (our choice).

### Refunding

There is no special mechanism (from our point of view) for refunding instalments. On Adyen’s side, if the amount that we send as a refund is higher than the amount settled, Adyen will accelerate capturing/settling of the money up to the refund amount, then refund the specified amount.

### Chargebacks

We were told that chargebacks on a purchase with instalments would count at a rate of 1 chargeback per settled instalment (instead of the usual 1 per purchase as a whole). This makes instalment purchases a bit riskier in terms of staying in the good graces of Visa’s and MasterCard’s and other card companies’ chargeback programs.

### How many instalments have settled?

We can only guess this through an approximation that 1 instalment will settle every month. There isn’t an explicit notification every time an instalment is settled. Accounting reporting may include this information, but it isn’t accessible via notifications or direct API calls.

## Argentina (dLocal / Spreedly)

[dLocal’s setup](https://docs.dlocal.com/api-documentation/payins-api-reference/payments/credit-card-payments/installments) works very differently. Instalments plan must be created in advance via API calls. These are not API calls that are part of the standard flow of payments, and therefore are not currently implemented/supported [by Spreedly](https://docs.spreedly.com/payment-gateways/d-local/) at the time of writing this document.

```sql
WHERE p.state = 'booked'

  AND g.installments_supported = true

ORDER BY 1 DESC, 2;
```

How to massively create Discount Codes: [https://github.com/busbud/napi/issues/6136#issuecomment-564242028](https://github.com/busbud/napi/issues/6136#issuecomment-564242028)

Discount codes don’t work on PMD sources **by design**: we don’t want to make accounting more complex. But [we don’t tell the user why](https://github.com/busbud/public-website/issues/9002).

## Legacy API

[Our current Cart API documentation](https://busbud-partners.readme.io/docs/cart-1) doesn't tell about discount codes. That's because it's a feature partner weren't supposed to use. Only Pubweb and the mobile apps we develop would—although there is no real protection for that.

Thus, the feature wasn't well documented.

Here's how it works, roughly.

<aside>
💡 The `currency` and `locale` query params are necessary for all Cart endpoints. They are used in the API response to convert the charges into the appropriate currency. If currency isn't provided, the default one will be determined based on the locale. If you provide nothing, everything will be converted to USD.

</aside>

### **Set a discount code**

- Endpoint `PUT /cart/:cart_id/discount?currency=CAD&locale=fr-CA` (adapt `currency` & `locale` to user preferences)
- You should pass `discount_code` in the body of the request (e.g. `{ "discount_code": "TESTMOBILE" }`)

Example:

```bash
curl --request PUT \\
  --url <https://napi-preview.busbud.com/cart/ZjUzZDU4NTAtNTY2Ny00ZT/discount?currency=CAD&locale=fr-CA> \\
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  --header 'x-busbud-token: GUEST_IfNBRGolTjGUf8EKQEbwKw' \\
  --data '{
	"discount_code": "TESTMOBILE"
}'
```

### **Unset a discount code**

- Endpoint `DELETE /cart/:cart_id/discount?currency=CAD&locale=fr-CA` (adapt `currency` & `locale` to user preferences)
