### Useful Commands

List of useful commands that are not easy to find in the above documentation. It also includes some of our own tooling such as `bb context` for switching your local config to point to the desired cluster.

Note these commands use the full length parameters such as `--namespace` to make things easier to understand. Feel free to check out the shorthands to make daily life with Kubernetes a lot easier using `--help` on any `kubectl` command.

```bash
# Switch local kubernetes context to point to the correct cluster for an adapter.
bb context ADAPTER

# Switch local kubernetes context to a specific integrations cluster region.
bb context REGION

# Download all available cluster contexts your Google account has access to.
bb download-contexts

# List all available cluster contexts.
kubectl config get-contexts

# Switch local kubernetes context to a specific cluster.
kubectl config use-context NAME

# Listing all pods in a cluster.
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces

# List pods in a specific namespace.
kubectl get pods --namespace=ADAPTER

# List all pods and the nodes they live on.
kubectl get pods -o wide --all-namespaces --sort-by="{.spec.nodeName}"

# Describing a pod to get environment variables, last crashes, etc.
kubectl describe pod --namespace=ADAPTER POD-ID

# Describe a ingress to see active IP, state, and health.
kubectl describe ingress --namespace=ADAPTER ADAPTER

# Temporary scale up/down a deployment. Modify the terraform script for a permanent scale.
kubectl scale deployment --namespace=ADAPTER ADAPTER --replicas=2

# Restart all pods for a deployment. (Note 'delete' in fact will restart pods)
# This will also reschedule pods if you're looking to manaully tell Kubernetes
# to try spreading out capacity across the cluster.
kubectl delete --all pods --namespace=ADAPTER

# Get history of deployments with revision numbers.
bb history ADAPTER

# Rollback last deployment.
kubectl rollout undo deployment/ADAPTER --namespace=ADAPTER

# Live tail logs
bb logs -a ADAPTER -f

# Get current CPU and memory usage of pods within a namespace
kubectl top pods -n NAMESPACE

# Enable debugging for a pod within a namespace.
kinspect NAMESPACE
kdeinspect NAMESPACE
```

### Taint a Terraform resource to be recreated

Terraform resources can be individually recreated if wanted. You can find a list of all the resources available in the [module’s terrform script](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/terraform-modules/tree/master/integration). Let’s take the example of wanting to recreate the Kubernetes ingress resource for Ouibus production.

```bash
# cd in to the integration directory
cd ouibus

# Taint the ingress resource, which marks it for recreation.
terraform taint -module=production kubernetes_ingress.default

# Apply changes
terraform apply -target=module.production

# Apply changes again, just incase some resources didn't receive changed information. In this case of recerating an
# ingress, Route 53 didn't get updated with the new IP.
terraform apply -target=module.production
```

### Moving application from one region to another

Moving an application across regions is a tad odd, but easily doable. Let’s take the scenario of wanting to move the `ouibus` integration from Europe to the US. Obviously modify the below steps to fit the integration and region you wish to work with.https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/namespaces/

1. Modify the region variable in `ouibus/main.tf` from `europe` to `us`.
2. `cd ouibus && bb deploy`
3. Get the external ip for the new service with `kubectl get service --namespace=ouibus`.
4. Wait at least 5 minutes after deploy for DNS TTL to expire. You can verify if DNS entries have updated with the new external ip with `dig int-ouibus.busbud-int.com`.
5. Switch context back to the original region, `bb context europe`.
6. Delete integration from old region with `kubectl delete namespace ouibus`.

### Resetting an application if Terraform is failing

If for whatever reason you’re finding yourself trying to delete an application (or recreate), and Terraform is causing you issues with state management, you can manually delete the application to reset Terraform’s state. **NOTE** this will obviously take the entire application offline, and will take 5-45 minutes to recreate Google’s load balancers.

Let’s take the scenario of us wanting to recreate Ouibus.

```bash
# Switch to the correct context.
cd ouibus
bb context ouibus

# Delete the entire Ouibus namespace and all the resources with it.
kubectl delete namespace ouibus

# Give kubernetes a few seconds to complete the task
sleep 5

# Run terraform destroy so it can verify that the resources were already deleted and update state.
terraform destroy

# Redeploy Ouibus
bb deploy
```

### How do I redeploy when using the latest tag?

When using `bb deploy` we automaticially create docker tag based on the last commit has for the integration. Sometimes when debugging we like to deploy branches and manually enter the tag `latest` to get our changes live. This however causes an issue where when `terraform apply` is run no changes are detected.

To get around this temporary issue, simply delete the pods after `bb deploy` has completed and they’ll be recreated with the latest docker tag.

```bash
kubectl delete --all pods --namespace=ADAPTER
```

### How do I add/remove a VM from a cluster?

It’s easiest to do this through the GKE UI.

1. Go to [GKE](https://console.cloud.google.com/kubernetes/list?project=busbud-integrations) and select the cluster you wish to modify.
2. Click `EDIT` at the top.
3. Scroll down to the `default-pool` at the bottom of the page, and modify the `size` input.
4. Save.

The VM will now automaticially be added/removed from the cluster.

- In the case of removing a VM, your pods will be rescheduled on to other VMs if there’s enough capacity (CPU/Memory).
- In the case of adding a VM, note pods may not be rescheduled right away on to the new VM. You can force this by deleting pods, which will have Kubernetes reevaluate capacity and spread the load across the new VM.

### I can’t deploy because of missing configuration block

If you encounter this kind of error message when you try to deploy:

```
Docker tag 20c7c346 for twelvego exists in the registry, skipping local build.
Deploying production
Acquiring state lock. This may take a few moments...
Releasing state lock. This may take a few moments...

Error: Error asking for user input: 1 error(s) occurred:

* module.development.module.app.kubernetes_deployment.default: configuration for module.development.module.app.provider.kubernetes is not present; a provider configuration block is required for all operations
```

It means that there was a `module` block in `main.tf`, which is now missing. Maybe you intentionally removed it, but now it’s blocking deployment because Terraform expects this resource to be present.

To solve this, we need to delete all the existing remote resources, and have Terraform update its state.

1. Recreate the development block in `main.tf`, you can do this by copying the `production` module block and replacing all instances of `production` with `development`.
2. Run `terraform init`
3. Run `terraform destroy -target=module.development`. If terraform asks for a commit variable, type in `latest`.
4. Remove the `development` module block from `main.tf`.

## Cache

To return results much faster and to avoid requesting departures too often to our partners API, Departure Service uses Redis to cache departures received from our partners. Sometimes the cache is polluted and needs to be cleaned. To do so, use the Departure Service [cache cleaner](https://github.com/busbud/departure-service/tree/master/tools/cache-cleaner) script.

## Common Issues

Here you’ll find common issues we face and how to solve them.

### Vault is sealed

If that happens, scale the Heroku dyno down and scale it back up again to reset the Postgres connections.

```bash
heroku ps:scale web=0 -a busbud-vaultsleep 10heroku ps:scale web=1 -a busbud-vault
```

### Vault Permission Denied

If you get a `permission denied` error, it is probably because your token has expired. You will need to run the login command again: `vault login -method=github token="$GITHUB_TOKEN"`.

### Updating a common dependency in all integrations

You can tweak the following `sed` command to update a dependency version for all integrations.

```bash
sed -Ei '' '/@busbud\/int/s/2\.[0-9]*\.[0-9]*/2.23.2/' */package.json
```

Then you need to run `yarn` in all integrations directories to make sure `yarn.lock` is in sync:

```bash
for x in */package.json; do (cd $(dirname "$x"); echo; echo "$x"; echo; yarn); done
```

You can then commit and push a branch.

If you would want to update a dependency only in TypeScript integrations:

```bash
for x in */tsconfig.json; do (cd $(dirname "$x"); echo; echo "$x"; echo; yarn); done
```

After updating dependencies like that, you might want to [mass deploy](integration/deployment.md#mass-deploy)

### Updating Node version used in integrations

To update the version of Node.js used to build and run integrations, you’ll need to change it in three places:

1. Change (or add) new Node versions to make Docker builds of the builder/runtime base images in the [`integrations/_tools/base_images`](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/master/_tools/base-images/Makefile) Makefile. Then run `make` to build and upload the new base images.
2. Set [`.nvmrc`](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/master/.nvmrc) in the integrations repo to match the new version that should be used.
3. Update the Node `engine` version in each integration’s `package.json` ([see example here](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/87488312d7b3c6fe29e976a7ea83c733455874e3/distribusion/package.json#L66-L68)). The version chosen here must correspond to an existing base image that was built and uploaded in step 1 or you will get an error on deployment.

After this, run a mass deploy and you’re set!

## Deprecating Imported Routes

It’s common for Bus partners to remove inventory from their backends. We handle this automatically except in the scenario when more than 20% of the total inventory is attempting to be removed. Engineering is notified of this in the `#integration-imports` slack channel with a message that looks like this:

![deprecated-routes.png](Maintenance/deprecated-routes.png)

To go ahead and rerun the task complete the following steps. We’ll use `flixbusus` as an example source.

1. Get the `batch_timestamp` for the last import from the [importer DB](https://github.com/busbud/integration-importer/blob/master/package.json#L14).

```sql
SELECT
  batch_timestamp - INTERVAL '1 DAY' AS batch_timestamp
FROM
  routes_partitioned
WHERE
  slug = 'flixbusus'
  AND env = 'production'
  AND batch_timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL '2 DAY'
ORDER BY
  1
LIMIT 1;
```

1. Set the returned value on the `sources.last_import_timestamp` for `flixbusus` within the Grand-Central database (`heroku pg:psql -a busbud-napi-prod`).
2. Rerun the import using the grunt command.

```bash
heroku run -a busbud-napi-prod -- 'cd apps/grand-central && npx grunt import:deprecate-routes:flixbusus'
```

# How to regenerate and resend undelivered tickets for multiple purchase IDs

A bug was preventing tickets (for multiple purchases) from being generated and from being sent? Here are the necessary steps to regenerate and resend them.

## What You’ll Need

---

- NAPI production token
- Connection details and credentials for the production bookie database (internal follower)
- Postgres database client

## Steps

---

1. Add a connection to the production bookie database within your database client.
2. Run the following query to list all the purchase IDs that have undelivered tickets, replacing `${start_date_time_of_bug}` with a date/timestamp that is before the occurrence of the issue:
    
    ```sql
    select id
    from purchases
    where created_at >= ${start_date_time_of_bug}
    and delivered_at is null
    and state = 'booked'
    order by trip_start_date asc;
    ```
    
3. Transfer the output of the previous query within a file. All purchase IDs should be line separated and unquoted.
4. From within your local bash shell, run the following command replacing `${purchase_id_file}` with the path to your file containing the purchase IDs and replacing `${napi_token}` with your production NAPI token:
    
    ```bash
    cat ${purchase_id_file} | \
    while read f;
    do 
    	curl -H "x-busbud-token:${napi_token}" "https://napi.busbud.com/purchases/$f/regenerate_tickets"
    done
    ```
    
5. After a few minutes of waiting once the previous command is complete, rerun the purchases query above from step 2 that selected the impacted purchases. Verify that the count is decreasing. This may take a few more minutes.
6. Share all purchase IDs that had their tickets successfully regenerated and resent, with any involved parties (usually just CX), by simply reposting on the related slack thread with the file.

## Done ✨

---

You’ve successfully regenerated and resent tickets for your purchase IDs!
filename: How to regenerate and resend undelivered tickets f.md

# On Call Guide

# Introduction

This guide will help you with the most common cases you may face when on call. Please add to it as you see fit as you go through your Helpdesk rotation.

## Getting Started

We have two primary roles for the “on call” employee:

1. **Helpdesk** - a [site reliability engineering (SRE)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Site_reliability_engineering)like role rotation in which the person on call:
    1. responds to internal support requests from other teams in the company in the [#helpdesk](https://busbud.slack.com/archives/CDLHQFT9V) channel on Slack,
    2. responds to external support requests from supply and demand partners via the [Partners Zendesk](https://busbud-partners.zendesk.com/agent/dashboard), and
    3. in their off time works to continuously improve the reliability of our software through bugfixes and foundational improvements, with an aim to improving and maintaining adherence to [primary service level objectives (SLOs)](https://app.datadoghq.com/slo).
2. **OpsGenie** - receiving and reacting to notifications from our alerting system when things go exceptionally wrong (“putting out fires”), such as downtime for a service, excessive failed bookings, and other symptoms of when we expend our error budgets allocated to service level objectives (SLOs).

# Helpdesk

*(formerly known as Rocket, or #platform-support)*

## Overview

The objective and scope of the Helpdesk rotation is as follows:

- Maintain site reliability and quality of experience at acceptable levels (sustainability)
- Minimize interruptions for rest of squad (super helpful!)
- Answer questions from peers and partners (super helpful!)

[RocketBot](https://github.com/busbud/rocketbot) will help you along by automatically managing Github issues for you based on incoming requests from Slack and Zendesk. Questions are to be answered based on what is a larger priority rather than first come first serve. You can use the `To do` column on the [Github board](https://github.com/orgs/busbud/projects/272) to sort the incoming tasks.

| In scope | Out of scope |
| --- | --- |
| Maintain SLOs at acceptable levels (reliability)
Improve SLO coverage
Fix bugs not covered by SLOs but should be (reliability)
Fix quality bugs impacting user experience (quality)
Fix issues impacting % sellable results (no results)
Tasks on the Helpdesk board in Github | Any tasks that can be easily planned and prioritized
Enhancements and features
New integrations/doc reviews
Feature completeness
Maintenance
“Large” tasks |

<aside>
💡 Make sure to wrap up sprint work prior to starting your week on Helpdesk!

</aside>

## Ending your Helpdesk shift

On the following Monday morning if there are any left over Helpdesk issues that you were not able to get to in time, be sure to:/ 

- Finish up any issues that can be tackled quickly (~5 minutes).
- Sync up with the next person on Helpdesk for your team to hand off remaining issues and answer any related questions.
- **Everything in the Blocked column should be empty at the end of your shift, so:**
    - **Move everything urgent or actionable to the Todo column**
    - **Move everything not-urgent but still blocking someone on the team to the Backlog for grooming**
    - Close any ticket where suppliers have not responded and it is only a nuisance or we are really unlikely to prioritize it if it were to go into the backlog.
- Reassign all remaining Github issues to the next person on call.

# Internal Support (`#helpdesk`)

- When you are going to check an issue reported on Slack’s channel #helpdesk, react with the eyes emoji (:eyes:) to let people know you are looking into it
- Once you are done and the issue is resolved, remove the eyes reaction and add the check emoji (:white_check_mark:).
- [RocketBot](https://github.com/busbud/rocketbot) will handle managing Github issues and moving them between the `To do`, `In Progress`, and `Done` columns. You can use the `To do` column on the [Github board](https://github.com/orgs/busbud/projects/272) to prioritize and organize your tasks.

## What if the task isn’t assigned to the right person or team?

Reassign it with `@Rocketbot reassign <team-slug>` Example: `@Rocketbot reassign revenue-innovation` .

## How do I prioritize tasks to respond to?

There are often more requests that come in than we can respond to in a timely manner. Best advice is to prioritize your efforts by category of request. At this time, those are, **in the following order**:

1. **🔥 Website Outage**: if true, drop everything (even what you’re currently working on) and triage or address.
2. **🐞 Bug Report (affecting >5 users)**: follow the usual mantra below
3. **💰 Payment Issues**: follow the usual mantra below
4. **🚌 Supply Missing or Inaccurate**: if the user didn’t run Doctor, run it for them. After that, if it’s a technical issue we need to solve, follow the usual mantra; otherwise it’s often a mapping issue so reassign it to `@supply-qa-help` with `@Rocketbot reassign supply-qa`
5. **📞 Partner Request**
6. **🧠 Request for Data**
7. **❓ General Question**
8. **🤷‍♀️ Other**

If there are pending issues, run through them in the above order, rather than the order in which they were filed.

If the issue is miscategorized by the requester, treat it in the order of the type it actually is (or as close as you can get). 

## What do I do with issues filed here?

The **Usual Mantra™️** is as follows:

1. Read the issue.
2. If the issue is related to an ongoing incident, flag to the person who is currently on call (OpsGenie).
3. Else, if the issue can be solved in 15 minutes or less, great! Take care of it ASAP, then close.
4. Else, if the issue cannot be solved in 15 minutes or less, add to the sprint board and we will assess its priority and schedule during grooming.

These steps are for your own protection. As indicated [above](On Call Guide.md), a Helpdesk shift can get very busy, and it’s not that we don’t want to immediately fix everything that we come across and be **#superhelpful** all the time, it’s simply that we can’t - or else we’re constantly neglecting other priorities. So please try hard to respect the Usual Mantra whenever you can.

## Route-Related Issue

*Common Forms Include:*

- *“We should be showing x route for y operator but we aren’t!”*

Most cases can be solved using [Doctor](about:blank#doctor)

If doctor does not have the route, but the locations exist, you can run doctor with a `dora=true` flag at the end of your flowbot doctor command, which will add the new route if departures exist. If Dora does find an entry you can ask flowbot to import the source (e.g `@Flowbot import biletall`), and then wait ~30 minutes for the process to complete in the background.

If Doctor was successful in fixing the problem, be sure to educate the user on how to use Doctor to investigate the problems themselves in the future.

If not successful based on what Doctor said, you may need the following actions:

1. Check on [BackOffice](https://backoffice.busbud-int.com/dashboard) whether we have the locations.
2. Check [napi database](about:blank#databases) whether we have the route.
3. Consider thinking of it as an [Integration Issue](about:blank#integration-issue)
4. Check the [Decision Tree](about:blank#decision-tree) to see if the problem should be moved to a normal issue on the grooming board.

### Trips for recently activated route not available

In some cases Doctor give the following diagnosis:

- *"There are X trips filtered due to flex cache not being updated. Come back in an hour."*

A quick fix is to purge the Fastly cache for Flex:

```bash
cd flex
yarn fastly:purge
# choose the environment and `flex-resolve-type:direct` option
```

## Integration Issue

*Common Forms include:*

- *“I can’t get any departures from x source!”*
- *“No tickets are being generated for x source!”*
- *“…is x source down?”*

First off, check if the integration’s pods are having problems through [Kubernetes](about:blank#kubernetes)

Most reliably, you can check [Sentry](about:blank#sentry) for errors on the integrations. Usually you will see recurring errors and an error spike. Click on the error and further investigate. If the sentry error comes from a booking flow call, it’ll also have a purchase-id, which you can then throw into [Support Tool](about:blank#support-tool) or our [logs](about:blank#logs-lots-of-them).

You can also go to Datadog to check request failure rates from both the requester and BELa.

<aside>
💡 *Sometimes the partner API is erroring, but some partners don’t use HTTP codes correctly, which means that their response is a HTTP 200, but the body has an error. You should remember to check BELa metrics as well.*

</aside>

<aside>
💡

</aside>

If they are asking about the inherent behaviour of a specific source (transfer not displayed, trip duration is incorrect etc), you can check to see if this question’s been seen before here:

[The Book Of Supply Red Tape (BETA)](../Shared%20Notes/The%20Book%20Of%20Supply%20Red%20Tape%20(BETA)%208fb9dccf0d1a4e87b6e343ae5b465e9d.md)

## Issue with Purchase Id (Order Number)

*Common forms include:*

- *“This one passenger had x problem with their purchase. <support tool link>”*

From the Support Tool link, we get the purchase-id, which we can then go find the [purchase-logs](about:blank#logs-lots-of-them) for.

From Support Tool, we can also search for similar successful bookings from the same source and cross-reference to find differences in the two bookings.

If we need to contact the partner, we can create a gist of the problem by adding a `--gist` flag at the end of our purchase-logs command.

If you would like a gist of a single log output, you can also copy it to your clipboard and run `pbpaste | bb upload-gist`.

## Duplicate booking/payment

Some possible causes of duplicate booking/payment for a user:

1. Pure technical issues such as: the client made duplicate requests, the server processed the purchase twice, or any other concurrency like issue. This can be identified by looking at the purchase timestamps
2. Layer 8 issues such as users closing the tab prematurely and thinking the booking didn't got through
3. and most likely, we made the user think that the booking failed when it was actually in progress or booked. There are multiple possible causes to this (connection errors, client side bugs, server side bugs, etc) and there's a bet to [prevent duplicate bookings](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1uj9y78BJ9IfumNJxnB9xDAghKj1xiGmrBl8dcMN4tD0/edit).

We can also inspect the user's behavior through Amplitude. We can find a link to the user's Amplitude profile in the Support Tool, with the user info.

## Debugging Searches on Busbud.com

*Common forms include:*

- *“This departure should be showing up but it isn’t!”*

If you need to debug a request for getDepartures on the adapter from a busbud.com search, you can try to get the request_id from the browser console:

On your browser, open the console and type `BB.inst.request_id` to get the request id. If you have the [Busbud Chrome Extension](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/busbud-extension/pfajipfmglejenikefknndcfojmhanol) you can also just hit `copy` in the `Request ID` row at the top to get the request_id

Then, you can use this request_id number to filter logs on GDS:

`bb adapter-logs <adpater_name> <request_id>`.

From there, you can see if the partner actually sent us departures or not.

## Problems Generating Finance Reports

Common forms include:

- “Generating sales report in busplatform site”
- “Sales reports are not being generated”
- “Errors when generating reports”

There are two main problems that causes reports from erroring:

### 1: Worker is crashing

Some reports take a lot of resources and can crash the workers. Bookies’ `bookie-reporting-worker` is the worker responsible for it. You can see if the pod is restarting, and also check the Bookie’s datadog dashboard to understand if memory/CPU are to blame.

One quick work around it to clear the [messages](https://dramatic-jaguar.rmq.cloudamqp.com/#/queues/rlpqzxqf/bookie-sales_reports_requests), restart the pods with more resources. But, sometimes reports states are saved as errors, and the worker will not try to generate a new one, which leads to cause number 2:

### 2: Report errored and is locked

All reports are saved on a google cloud storage [bucket](https://console.cloud.google.com/storage/browser/bookie-reports-production/sales/on-demand?pageState=("StorageObjectListTable":("f":"%255B%255D"))&authuser=0&project=busbud-integrations&prefix=&forceOnObjectsSortingFiltering=false)

Sometimes, failed reports are saved as errors on the bucket and the worker won’t try to regenerate it. The fix is to delete the problematic report on the GCS page. The easiest way to find the problematic report is by checking the creation date, and the first number on the report name - which is the source ID. Deleting it should allow the report to be regenerated.

## Add someone to Backoffice

Follow this documentation : [https://www.notion.so/thebusbudgroup/How-do-I-give-access-in-Backoffice-919bd559ca3e4ae29c49ba13f69bacf2](../FAQs/How do I give access in Backoffice.md)

<aside>
💡

The user permissions are cached and are only updated when we grant or revoke permissions. 

So if you're having issues adding someone to Backoffice (a common symptom is a black/blank screen), add/remove one permission in order to update the cache.

</aside>

## Revoking user access to our tools

1. Get the user’s email address
2. Remove email from the Support Tool config if present: [https://github.com/busbud/busbud-support/blob/master/infra/production/main.tf#L48](https://github.com/busbud/busbud-support/blob/master/infra/production/main.tf#L48), merge the change and redeploy the app.
3. In Backoffice, head over to the admin [Access Management](https://backoffice.busbud-int.com/dashboard/admin?tab=Access+Management) section, toggle the “Revoke Access” checkbox, enter the user’s email below and click “Delete access”.
4. You’re done. ✨

## Performance Issues

*Common forms include:*

- *“SupportTool is reaaaaallllllyyyyyy sloooooooow todayyyyyyyy”*
- *“BusPlatform isn’t loading”*

First off, you have to be able to reproduce the issue. If you aren’t able to reproduce it, ask for the specific set of actions that the person did to get the problem. If no one else can reproduce the problem, it’s probably not a problem.

After that, a good place to start is in Chrome Developer Tools:

- Fire up the network tab and reload the page to see if any network requests are taking an absurdly long amount of time
- Unlikely, but you can also go to the performance tab, click on the record button, then load up the page again to see if any frontend rendering is being absurdly slow

<aside>
💡 For performance problems, remember to pay attention to cache as it will make things faster

</aside>

## No LOTR data on preview

*Common forms include:*

- *“I can’t find any LOTR data on preview. Is something broken?”*

We have a kubernetes scheduler that runs [this](https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/8605aac85c50289b4dd53498f106fedeac58ed49/apps/grand-central/tools/database-restore/database-sync-local.sh#L1-L52) script on grand-central-preview in the `busbud-us-east4-1` that restores the preview database every friday evening. Sometimes, this job fails, resulting in no preview data.

### Re-run restore

Usually a re-run of the script will fix the issue:

- Open the `grand-central` project from `napi` repo, and add or export the database url for the preview environment.
- You can then run the yarn command `db:production:preview:restore`
- Confirm data was restored. You can connect to the preview database and run this query `SELECT * from sources where id < 0` (Since LOTR data has negative IDs).
- If autocomplete does not work on pubweb, follow the instructions on the [Flex repo README](https://github.com/busbud/flex) to sync the preview database for tables `search_suggestions_v2` and `interconnected_city_routes`.

### Rollback restore

The script for restoring is atomic and it generally sections out to three steps.

1. Restore to a temp table
2. Backup existing database and rename the temp to current
    
    <aside>
    💡 In this section you can rename the old table back to the current one, that is the fastest way to keep it active
    
    </aside>
    
3. Run post restore scripts
    
    <aside>
    💡 In this instance, you’ll have to ssh into the kubernetes pods and rerun the post restore script command `yarn db:preview:test-data`
    
    </aside>
    

## Non Supply member needs to contact a partner

Ping the operations manager for the region in the Slack thread to help out.for

## Issues with generating bookie reports from Back Office

- *“It takes forever to generate a report”*.
- *“I can’t generate a report for operator X.”*

When there are support requests regarding potential issues with generating reports, here are some quick things that you can do:

- Look at the requested report generation date range. If the range is large (more than a month), ask user to segment their report into smaller date ranges. Reports should be capped at a month range ideally.
- Verify message count within the queue `bookie-sales_reports_requests` using the RabbitMQ manager view and purge messages. *How?* Through the [CloudAMQP dashboard](https://customer.cloudamqp.com/instance), select the queue `queue-production-eu` and then click on the RabbitMQ manager button on the top left. Within the RabbitMQ manager page, look for the “Queues” tab and search for the queue. Select it and verify queue state. You should see a “Purge” section lower on the page which will give you the option to purge messages from the queue. Click the “Purge Messages” button to purge all messages from the queue.
- If any, delete all lock files from within the GCS bucket [bookie-reports-production](https://console.cloud.google.com/storage/browser/bookie-reports-production/sales/on-demand;tab=objects?pageState=(%22StorageObjectListTable%22:(%22f%22:%22%255B%255D%22))&project=busbud-integrations&prefix=&forceOnObjectsSortingFiltering=false).
- From the [Datadog Bookie dashboard](https://app.datadoghq.com/s/b53086d55/jy3-pkd-t72), look at the system metrics for `bookie-reporting-worker`. It could indicate that you need to increase some resource limits (cpu, or memory).

## Creating or editing Demand Partners

Rocket can receive requests for the creation and maintenance of **Demand Partners**.

### Resolving a conflicting Partner/Source ID

Finance considers Demand Partners and Sources as Vendors; and therefore they are stored on the same table on Netsuite and cannot have conflicting IDs.

Due to this limitation, we updated partners to use different IDs to prevent conflicts, so today Partners have IDs starting at 100xxx, and Sources have IDs starting at 3xxx. But, from time to time we receive requests of old Partner being reactivated or reused; this causes conflicts on Netsuite and requires us to manually update the PK on the Partners table. There’s a checklist that should cover everywhere that needs to be updated:

[https://www.notion.so/thebusbudgroup/Update-Partner-ID-19229aab919980168eafe752e85b16bf](../Guides & Checklists/Update Partner ID.md)

## An employee is pressuring to solve an issue in an specific or time constraint way

Every team has different priorities that may differ from ours. This is common and totally appropriate! However we must also stick to our existing rule sets when evaluating issues. Some common issues we face:

- When a company is moving between integrations that were asked to “be quick and assist” on the transition. It’s important to keep in mind that we are not an external partners QA team, and they are to be ready and live in production before we make any changes.
- A team is dependant on our stack and finds a bug that may be causing them issues in production. It’s important to understand and evaluate the priority of the problem first, as just because an issue is being reported internally does not make it a fire.

For any concerns related to this process, be sure to reach out the Tech Lead on call with you to discuss!

## Location / routes are not imported

If someone is ensuring that the partner returns routes that are not present in our system it could be because the import process experiences an issue

There are three parts in the import process

1. The integration
2. [The importer DB](https://github.com/busbud/integration-importer): Holds locations and routes returned by the integration
3. [NAPI imports](https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/master/apps/grand-central/lib/importer.js): Transforms the location and routes from 2 into Xmappings

**Tips**

- The importer DB has information about the source status
`select * from sources where slug='<source_slug>';` to view last_fail , last_start, last_run. These will tell you if when the import job ran successfully for the last time
`select xid, created_at from history_import_locations where slug='<source_slug>' order by created_at desc limit 20;` to view the latest imported locations. If the xmapping listed is not listed here then the integration is not returning it
`select * from routes_partitioned_<source_slug> order by created_at desc limit 20;` Same as above but for routes
- If the expected information is not listed here you should look at the integration logs to see why it’s not being returned. It could be either because there’s a bug in the adapter or because the supplier’s API is not returning it. If the former, fix the bug; if the latter contact the partner.
- If you want to know if the importer DB is in sync with NAPI you can run the [db-compare](https://github.com/busbud/integration-importer/tree/master/tools/db-compare) script
- If you know that importer DB contains information that NAPI doesn’t you can trigger a NAPI import by doing
`kubectl -n grand-central-production exec deploy/grand-central-import-worker-production -- yarn grunt import:full:<source_slug>`
    - Alternatively you can import only locations or only routes with `import:locations:<source_slug>` or `import:routes:<source_slug>`
    - If the import fails you can debug it with `BUSBUD_ENV=production NAPI_TOKEN=$NAPI_PROD_TOKEN yarn grunt import:locations:<source_slug>`

# OpsGenie: or, the Art of Putting Out Fires

![](http://i.imgur.com/6NfmQ.jpg)

Alright calm down, take a breath. Shit breaks all the time, hell, it may even fix itself before you get a chance to finish reading this doc. If it doesn’t however, this explains the common scenarios we face with integration and infrastructure issues, and likely where the alerts are coming from.

First things first, remember you have these tools at your disposal when debugging.

- The integrations root domain to get it’s current status code. Eg. `NAME.busbud-int.com`.
- `bb logs NAME -f` to get real time logs for an integration.
- [`bb gcs-logs`](maintenance.md#logs) for logging in to the log VM and searching through past logs
- `kubectl` for accessing Kubernetes resources (more details in the error descriptions).
- [Sentry](maintenance.md#error-tracking) for error tracking.
- [The support tool](https://support.busbud-int.com/) gives you quick insights on failing purchases and what kind of errors to look for in Sentry.

To make life easier, before you start debugging run `bb context NAME` to make sure your local kubernetes context is pointing to correct cluster. Without setting the correct cluster, you won’t be able to interact with your integration’s resources.

## How important is this adapter?

Our opsgenie alerts are tiered by the amount of sales and revenue they generate, so a P2 alert for an adapter will always be more important that a P3 alert for a different adapter.

Note that we currently don’t have P1 alerts for integrations. If you need to compare important between two P2 integration alerts, you can check the daily posts by flowbot on the #main channel in slack for the top 10 ranking, otherwise just tackle in alert order

## Integration is 500ing

*(Stackdriver + OpsGenie)*

The integration is likely crashing due to bad code, or the partner making a breaking change. Questions to ask:

### Have you tried turning it off and on again?

![turnitoff.gif](On%20Call%20Guide/turnitoff.gif)

Yeah, I know what you’re thinking, but you’d be so surprised on how often that works.

- Run `kubectl rollout restart deployment/DEPLOYMENT_NAME -n NAMESPACE_NAME` to restart all pods. List of deployment for a namespace : `kubectl get deployments -n NAMESPACE_NAME`
- After the command exits, wait 5 seconds and then check `int-ADAPTER_NAME.busbud-int.com` (e.g. `https://int-moveliaudm.busbud-int.com`) to see if your integration is up.
    - `int-ADAPTER_NAME-dev.busbud-int.com` for development adapters (e.g. `https://int-moveliaudm-dev.busbud-int.com`)

If you find this successful then great, the fire is out. However you should continue investigating on why it happened to prevent it in the future.

### When was the last deploy and by who?

- For integrations, run `bb history` in the integration folder.
- For other services, `kubectl describe deployment --namespace=NAME` to get the latest deploys.

Was the deploy done within last hour? Sounds like someone may have screwed up. Ask to find out. If you got no answer and the start time of the error increase lines up with the deploy, then roll it back with `kubectl rollout undo --namespace=NAME deployment/NAME`.

This can also be accomplished through our quick access at the Rollback link on the release message (`#releases` channel on Slack).

![Untitled](On%20Call%20Guide/Untitled%202.png)

Time to create a proper incident on [incido](https://incidents.busbud-int.com/incidents)! These incidents can be also checked at the `#platform-incident-status` Slack channel.

Now go to the corresponding source page on [Backoffice](https://backoffice.busbud-int.com/dashboard/bus-company/sources), Outages tab and create a new one.

## Common Alerts

### [IS or PS or Flex] Availability

This alert means we’ve seriously depleted our error budget for Inventory or Poll Services or Flex. These are generally *high priority* problems meaning a total outage of DS/PS/Flex in a region, a failed deploy or a serious bug affecting one of those applications.

- Check service history on the service’s dashboard in [Datadog](about:blank#datadog) to see if any particular metrics are spiking, or if it is an ongoing or already-solved issue
- Check the pod status and/or logs in [Google Cloud](https://console.cloud.google.com/kubernetes/application?project=busbud-integrations) and with `kubectl get pods -n service-name --context cluster-name` / `kubectl logs -n service-name pod-name --context cluster-name`
- Check for spikes in errors [in the associated Sentry project](about:blank#sentry)

### [INT] Availability

When this alert is triggered, the first thing we could do is treat it as an integration issue, go to [Google Cloud](https://console.cloud.google.com/kubernetes/application?project=busbud-integrations) and search for the integration. Then, check [Sentry](about:blank#sentry) and [Datadog](about:blank#datadog) for possible errors that should be handled.

Another good place to go is [Support Tool](about:blank#support-tool) and check for booking errors - and which booking errors. If there’s an error, you can probably see it on the support tool, sentry and datadog. Then, use [GCS Logs](about:blank#logs-lots-of-them) to further understand it and take appropriate action.

The error might be happening because some types of errors are miscategorized as `OperationalError`s or `<Adapter Name>APIError`s instead of a more appropriate value like `SelectedSeatsNotAvailable` or `PassengerAnswersInvalid`. The metric is intended to only track exceptions, that is to say: bugs in our code or in the partner’s environment. We should therefore make sure any error that can be thrown as a `BusbudError`, is thrown as such.

Lastly, it could just be that the partner API is busted. Find evidence of this in the GCS Logs (as ideas, you can grep for the reoccuring error, or the purchaseID if you have any), and contact the partner

Alerts triggered for this type of issue will close themselves once the error budget recovers sufficiently, which may take a couple of days.

### LetsEncrypt Cert has less than 14 days until it expires

<aside>
💡 *If you get many of these notifications at the same time, more than likely it’s because someone on the team messed up and/or are moving things around. Consult anyone on the team who you know has been playing around with our kubernetes infrastructure and ask if they know anything about it. If no one knows anything…then you are on your own!*

</aside>

Check the Datadog monitor on the OpsGenie alert, confirm the certificate data truly has less than 14 days. If it is showing some negative amount of days left, the script for calculating is probably busted. Re running the job that produces the stat may fix it

```bash
kubectl create job --from=cronjob/letsencrypt-statsd "letsencrypt-statsd-$(date +%s)" -n cert-manager
```

You can also do a few things to check validity: `kubectl describe certificates -n <integration name>` This will give you the expiry date of the certificate under “status”.

You can also go into [Google Cloud Platform](about:blank#kubernetes-and-gcp) and click on “Lets Encrypt, Certificate Details” to the right-hand side.

If it is valid and is going to truly expire in less than 14 days, it means the cert-manager is not automatically renewing it like it should be. We can get its logs by doing `kubectl get pods -n cert-manager` and use the pod name that is only “cert-manager-<id>” to do `kubectl logs -n cert-manager <pod-name> -f` to get its logs, and work from there.

### Ticket Validation Failed for XX

<aside>
💡 Currently, we are not checking for operators - so most alerts will be for tickets that are different, but it’s because they are from different operators. In this case we don’t need to worry about the alert.

</aside>

When you receive an alert for a ticket validation issue it could mean the following:

1. New generated tickets file sizes deviates from the average size
2. New generated tickets file diffs from a master ticket above a threshold

In order to further debug this, the best place to go is check logs on `gcs-mounts` as part of our [GCS logs](about:blank#logs-lots-of-them).

Go to `/gcs-mounts/busbud_logs/bookie` and look for **validateTicket** issues (`cat * | grep validateTicket`). The logs will contain the following information:

- Error
- Purchase ID
- Source ID
- Extra error information, depending on which error occurred (such as a list of URLs that were used to compare size/diff, pdf urls, and other)

The error message indicates the issue:

- **Ticket size deviates from median ticket size for source XX**
    - In this case, the file size deviates from the average. Note that the average value is for a single passenger - so if the ticket is for multiple passengers, the median value will be the size / number of passengers. This information is logged (number of passengers, calculated median size) to assist you when debugging.
    - !!! info “For Greyhound…” Greyhound has random values for their ticket sizes, so we may have to ignore some greyhound alerts for size deviation.
- **Ticket file has different number of pages for source XX**
    - This error doesn’t trigger alerts. There are some cases where a ticket has an extra page, but it’s because the content didn’t fit so the last line of the document goes to a new page. It could indicate a problem if the same purchase_id errored for size/diff.
- **Ticket diff comparison is above threshold for source XX**
    - This error means that the PDF file comparison (which converts the PDF to an image and performs an image analysis to compare both images) gave a mismatch above the threshold. In order to debug it, logs will have the master_url, which is the url for the ticket used in the comparison. You’ll also have the purchase_id, which you can use to check the generated ticket and compare them. It could indicate an issue with the ticket, or it could indicate that the threshold we have is not high enough.

### EAI_AGAIN or queryA ETIMEOUT

If you’re seeing one or more integrations throwing error `EAI_AGAIN` in Sentry no matter the domain, it’s likely due to KubeDNS [taking too long to respond to DNS queries](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/issues/2866). There’s currently a temporary patch in place that reboots KubeDNS daily through a Kubernetes Cronjob, however if that doesn’t work you can run the following yourself.

```bash
bb context CLUSTER
kubectl get pods -n kube-system | grep 'kube-dns' | grep -v autoscaler | awk -F' ' '{print $1}' | while read pod; do kubectl delete pod -n kube-system $pod; done;
```

You can monitor KubeDNS and its response time through the [Integration KubeDNS Dashboard](https://app.datadoghq.com/dash/810681/integrations-kubedns).

There could also be a problem with `k8s-gcs-logger` which has a healthy appetite for file watchers and often causes issues in the cluster with other apps that use file watchers, in this case `kube-dns`. You can try running the same steps as above but for namespace `k8s-gcs-logger`.

Silverrail payments are done via a Busbud Credit Card that gets passed to their API. We have one credit card for amtrak and one for Viarail.

Upon receiving continuous payment errors, first check with the finance team if our credit card was maxed out. You can do this by simply pinging Viktoria on slack: 

[https://busbud.slack.com/archives/CDLHQFT9V/p1714160174492059?thread_ts=1714153192.955109&cid=CDLHQFT9V](https://busbud.slack.com/archives/CDLHQFT9V/p1714160174492059?thread_ts=1714153192.955109&cid=CDLHQFT9V)

### When do I push my emergency patch?

Let’s take a scenario. It’s 3am on a Saturday, Val is still drunk and not very responsive, yet you’ve just put together a quick patch to fix 30% of sales on Transdev (an integration he wrote). You’re expecting your patch to work, you’ve tested it locally and everything seems right, but you have little knowledge on how Transdev works. Do you deploy your fix?

Generally, the answer is yes. There’s a few steps you should take after you’ve deployed:

1. Commit your code. Always. It doesn’t matter the time of day. If someone pushes another patch after you have and your codebase is not in sync, we’ll start seeing regressions.
2. Ping all the integration developers about what you’re doing, your code changes, and why. That way when they’re available they’re aware the of the situation.
3. **Monitor**. Monitor sales success rate on Datadog, make sure there’s no new errors on Sentry and the one you were fixing reduces.
4. Mark any OpsGenie alerts as solved. That way if your patch ends up not working after you’ve stopped monitoring, you’ll get notified again.
5. Go back to real life.

## Kubernetes and GCP

Check if the integration has been having issues with constant restarts, or the pods are down in general. Constant restarts may indicate a bigger underlying problem.

To do this there are two ways:

### CLI

- Run `kubectl get pods --namespace=NAME` to get all the pods for the integration or service. Make sure you are using the proper context (integrations operate in `busbud-int-us` and `busbud-int-eu`, other services in `busbud-us-east4-1` and `busbud-eu`; switch like so: `bb context busbud-int-us`).

Example:

```
NAME                      READY     STATUS              RESTARTS   AGE
acn-cmd-816404425-78grl   0/1       CrashLoopBackoff    7          1d
acn-cmd-816564425-gg23r   1/1       Running             2          1d
```

- Copy the pod name that has multiple restarts or is in the middle of crashing and describe it. You’ll need to prefix the podname with `po/` when running describe. This will output a lot of information, but the points you want to look at are `Containers -> Last State`. There you’ll be able to see the reason for the last exit, and continue debugging.

In the example below, you’ll see that the `acn` integration exited with exit code 1, meaning that something in the integration itself caused it to quit rather then an external source. Other times you’ll find it with error codes like `137 OOMKILLED` specifying the integration ran out of memory and was forcibly killed. You can increase your resource limit by passing them to your integrations terraform script. See [`terraform-modules/integration/main.tf`](https://github.com/busbud/terraform-modules/blob/master/integration/main.tf) for all the possible parameters and defaults.

### Web UI

![gcp-2.png](On%20Call%20Guide/gcp-2.png)

If you click on deployment, you will see the status of the pods. There are links to its corresponding datadog and sentry on the right side as well.

# Contour is not routing traffic

First step, take a breath! This will get patched up quick.

Contour not routing traffic from past experiences is due to the GRPC TLS cert that’s Contour uses to speak to Envoy has expired. Before going in depth, let’s be sure to check that first!

1. Switch to the cluster context where you’re experiencing issues.
2. Run the following command to get the TLS expiry date.

```bash
kubectl config use-context YOUR-CLUSTER
kubectl get secret -n contour envoycert -o json | jq -rc '.data["tls.crt"]' | base64 -D | openssl x509 -enddate -noout -in /dev/stdin
```

You’ll see a response such as the following:

```bash
notAfter=Sep  3 13:10:54 2023 GMT
```

If this date is in the past, than we’ve found the problem and you’re in the right place! Otherwise, you’ll need to investigate further with others on the team.

If you’re on a Mac, you’ll need to install GNU sed first.

```bash
brew install gnu-sed
```

We’ll use a script below in order to generate a new cert that will live for 20 years. It gets the version of Contour currently installed, downloads the job schema from Github that will generate the cert, and applys!

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Get the contour version currently installed.
export CONTOUR_VERSION=$(kubectl get ds -n contour -o yaml | grep 'contour:' | awk -F ':' '{print $3}' | awk -F '-' '{print $1}' | head -n 1)

# Delete left over pods, outdated certificate secrets.
kubectl delete --all job -n contour
kubectl delete secret -n contour envoycert
kubectl delete secret -n contour contourcert

# 1. Set correct namespace
# 2. Duplicate an argument that's used in contour certgen command
# 3. Replace duplicate argument with certificate lifetime
# 4. Apply
curl -L "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/projectcontour/contour/v${CONTOUR_VERSION}/examples/contour/02-job-certgen.yaml" |
	gsed 's/namespace: projectcontour/namespace: contour/g' |
	gsed '/--overwrite/{p;}' |
	gsed '0,/--overwrite/s/--overwrite/--certificate-lifetime=7300/' |
	kubectl apply -f -

# Wait for job to finish
while ! (kubectl get pods -n contour | grep certgen | grep -q "Completed"); do sleep 1; done

# Delete completed job, restart all pods.
kubectl delete --all job -n contour
kubectl delete --all pods -n contour --force --grace-period=0

# Verify new expiry date
kubectl get secret -n contour envoycert -o json | jq -rc '.data["tls.crt"]' | base64 -D | openssl x509 -enddate -noout -in /dev/stdin
```

The script will output the expiry date at the end, it should be far-far in the future. Verify Contour is now properly routing traffic, and you’re done!

# Geo Entity Orphaned

## Description

This alerts occur when the auto-heal script for managing hierarchies in [geo-service](Geo Entity Orphaned.md) fails. The script is designed to look at our closure table and figure out if there are any geo-entities that are not attributed in a hierarchy.

The alert occurs when a worker called `entity-check` fails, this worker runs every 2 hours in geo-service. If you come across the alert you can do the following to resolve issues.

## **Prerequisites**

- Familiarity with geo-service is a plus, you can check the [spec](Geo Entity Orphaned.md) in the appendix
- You need to be able to connect to a database using any client. The procedure to connect to the database for geo-service is in the readme [here](Geo Entity Orphaned.md).
- If the age of the alert is greater then 2 hours, you can skip to [this](Geo Entity Orphaned.md) step to double check as the worker may have re-run and auto healed the issue.

## Procedures

1. Connect to database
    1. You can leverage this [readme](Geo Entity Orphaned.md) to connect to the geo-service database, EU instance is a replica and the primary is in the US.
    2. Once, connected the relevant tables to keep track of are `geo_entity` and `geo_entity_closure` 
2. Query for geo_entity
    1. You want to make queries to the `geo_entity` table by running the below query and appending the id’s that appeared on the opsgenie alert, we want to see the `type`, `metadata` and `id`
        
        ```jsx
        SELECT metadata, id, type
        FROM geo_entity
        WHERE id in ('<insert id here>', '<insert id here>')
        ```
        
    2. Geo entity can have different `metadata` information depending on the `type`. The current known ones are `city`, `location`, and `point-of-interest` . The `metadata` property of the table is json data type that stores legacy information, that will allow us to cross reference across multiple databases and existing data.
        1. We want to make sure that for each different type there is enough information available for us to accurately fix/heal the hierarchical relationships. So for each type we want to see that at-least the following is true.
            1. If the `type` is location, we should see a `city_id` in the `metadata` property.
            2. If the `type` is city, we should see a `region_id` in the metadata property.
            3. If the `type` is point of interest, we should see a `city_id` in the metadata property.
        2. The above information represents identifiers that we can use to figure out if the entity has relationships. Depending on if it’s `region_id` or `city_id` we want to check the `geo_entity` table to make sure this information exists.
            1. Make another query to `geo_entity` with the information about the metadata
                
                ```jsx
                -- for city_id
                SELECT metadata, id, type
                FROM geo_entity
                WHERE id in ('<insert id here>', '<insert id here>')
                
                -- for region_id
                SELECT metadata, id, type
                FROM geo_entity
                WHERE dbt_unique_key = 'region<insert region_id>' 
                ```
                
    
3. Fix the relationships
    1. At this point, it’s confirmed the `child` has `parents` that both exist. You can use the following query to fix the table. It will automatically rebuild the hierarchy all the way through.
        
        ```jsx
        INSERT INTO geo_entity_closure (ancestor_id, descendant_id, depth, relationship_type)
        SELECT
            p.ancestor_id,
            c.descendant_id,
            p.depth + c.depth + 1,
            'hierarchichal'
        FROM
            geo_entity_closure p,
            geo_entity_closure c
        WHERE
            p.descendant_id = '<this is the id of parent>'::uuid
          AND c.ancestor_id = '<this is the id of the child>'::uuid
        ON CONFLICT (ancestor_id,
            descendant_id,
            relationship_type)
            DO NOTHING;
        ```
        
        <aside>
        💡 The query is slightly confusing but, yes, the `descendant_id` should be the `parent` you want to link and the `ancestor_id` should be the `child` you want to link.
        
        </aside>
        

## Missing Data

If you have missing data or the hierarchy can not be formed due to the parent missing, then you’ll have to do the following.

1. Confirm data in grand central
    1. Depending on the type of geo entity you can go to the corresponding tables in grand central and query them.
        
        
        | geo-service (type) | grand-central (table) | Id to use |
        | --- | --- | --- |
        | location | locations | metadata.id |
        | city | cities | id (both geo entity and city id are the same across databases) |
        | point-of-interest | points_of_interests | metadata.city_id |
    2. If there is no data in grand central you can delete it in geo entity table.
    3. If there is data in grand central then there is likely duplication, you can query geo entity to see if you have multiple of the same by using various properties. You can use `geohash` and `type` to narrow it down. If there are two entries with the exact same properties for `geohash` and `type` delete the one that doesn’t have information in the `metadata` property.

## Confirm hierarchies

If you want to confirm if there is a hierarchy already in place for the affected id you can run the query below. If you see a gradual increase on the depth like so 0, 1, 2. It means hierarchical relationships were established and you can ignore the geo entity.

```jsx
select  ge.id, gec.ancestor_id, ge.metadata, ge.type, gec.depth
from geo_entity ge
join geo_entity_closure gec on gec.descendant_id = ge.id
where ge.id = 'id'
```

💡 Example: Note the depth filed has 0, 1, 2

# VIA Rail Payment Failures

## Scenario

All bookings for VIA Rail are failing with `PartnerAPIBlocked` errors and the following message: `An unknown error occurred during initiation of the payment`. 

## Context

We pay for our bookings with VIA Rail on a corporate card registered to Busbud. Payments on this credit card are made on a regular basis by the Finance team. At times, either through a missed or delayed payment or when the volume of bookings unexpectedly jumps such that we lose track of how much balance we have left on the card, it is possible that it runs out of available balance for making bookings. When this happens, the above error is thrown on every purchase.

## Solution

To recover from this, we must do three things:

1. **Set a source outage.** It should last for 24 hours (or longer if this happens on a Friday or over the weekend).
2. **Wait 24 hours** after the payment to the credit card was confirmed to have been applied. VIA Rail’s payment processor Moneris has a fraud velocity rule that applies an approximately 24-hour long delay for clearing out insufficient balance statuses on cards. That means that even if the payment is applied and we can use the card to pay for other things, it may still fail on VIA Rail bookings for up to 24 hours after.
3. **Reinitialize the payment data key** used for production bookings. The `payment_data_key` is used to tie our corporate card to the VIA Rail production environment. It must be reinitialized by performing a production booking on VIA Rail’s website using the corporate card number, then obtaining the token and saving it in the vault.
    1. After the 24-hour mark, go to [viarail.ca](http://viarail.ca) and create an account using your `@busbud.com` work email address.
    2. Log into the account and go through the purchase flow to make a one-way booking on a cheap route (e.g. Montreal to Ottawa 4 weeks out). Don’t worry about choosing a fancy refundable fare - VIA Rail has a policy where all bookings are fully refundable within 24 hours of purchase, even the cheapest ones.
    3. Once you get to the payment step, enter the payment details for the Busbud VIA Rail corporate card, available in Lastpass. If you don’t have read access for some reason, ask Dustin or Mike.
        1. For the billing address, you must use the following value:
        First name: **Busbud**
        Last name: **Buspayments**
        Address: **901-5425 av Casgrain500-1275 Av. des Canadiens-de-Montréal, Montréal QC H2T 1X6H3B 0G4**
        2. ⚠️ Make sure you click **“Save this payment information to my profile for future use.”** ← VERY important!
        3. Click “Book”
    4. If the booking was successful, open the Developer Tools of your browser and monitor XHR requests. Then, go into your dashboard (”My VIA Profile” > “Account Dashboard”).
    5. In your Developer Tools request list, look at a request made to `GET /wallet` . There will be a property in the response called `card_token`.
        
        ![Screenshot 2025-05-14 at 10.45.44.png](VIA%20Rail%20Payment%20Failures/Screenshot_2025-05-14_at_10.45.44.png)
        
    6. Update the Vault property for `SOURCE_CONFIG_viarail2` in the `sqills2` integration, and set `payment_data_key` to the value of `card_token` from the previous step. If there is no card token returned, it means you didn’t check to save payment information, go back to step b) and try again.
    7. Redeploy the integration.
    8. Cancel your booking made on [viarail.ca](http://viarail.ca) via your account dashboard.

## Cancellation and Refund

There are four types of cancellation response: `success`, `pending`, `denied` and `failed`. There are `orc_travel` departures available to simulate each state. You can use `Isengard` to `Barad-dur` route to find them:

- Use `Orc Travel REFUND DENIED` departure to get `denied` state
- Use `Orc Travel Valid` departure to get `success` state
- Use `Orc Travel TICKET NOT CANCELLABLE` departure to get `pending` state

There is no departure to simulate `failed` state because optimistic cancellation doesn't allow us to fail cancellation.

If you want to get `failed` state, here's what you can do:

1. Make a purchase with `Orc Travel TICKET NOT CANCELLABLE` departure
2. Try to cancel. It would set the cancellation state to `pending`
3. Go to Support Tool and refuse the cancellation. That would update the cancellaton state to `failed`

# Temporarily skip a Bookie E2E test

## Context

It could happen that you end up in a situation where some of your e2e test cases might fail on merging to master,
not because of a bug on Bookie but rather a bug on one of the services it depends on (e.g. Grand-central API endpoint down).

If what you want to release contains new changes which cannot wait for the bug to be fixed **AND** you're sure that
the e2e test cases failing have nothing to do with your release, then you can skip those test cases
temporarily.

## Steps

1. Go to the Circle CI job that failed and identify the failing testing cases for which you desire to skip the execution
2. Click on the `Project Settings` button in the top right corner of the Circle CI job page
    
    ![project-settings-ci.png](Test%20Scenarios/project-settings-ci.png)
    
3. Go to the `Environment Variables section` and add a new environment variable `BOOKIE_E2E_SKIP` with
the text which will filter out the test cases you wish to skip
    
    ![env-variable-section-ci.png](Test%20Scenarios/env-variable-section-ci.png)
    
4. Re-run the failed job and now your e2e tests should be passing
5. **Do not forget to delete the created environment variable once the bug has been resolved.**

# Background

Unlike most other microservices, bookie is in only EU cluster. The reason is due to GDPR compliance, which requires that the customers's data (originating from the EU) must be stored in the EU region.

The bookie's preview instance is in the US cluster. All clients' contract tests (e.g. pubweb's cypress tests) rely on bookie's preview instance to pass. When migrating the preview instance to GCP, we started off with assigning it to the EU cluster. We discovered a lot of timing out issues with pubweb's cypress tests. To resolve that, we moved the preview instance to the US cluster.

## GDPR

The customers' data in the bookie's DB are encrypted. All the info is documented [here](https://github.com/busbud/product/issues/82).

## Related links:

- Heroku to GCP Migration Epic: [https://github.com/busbud/napi/issues/8460](https://github.com/busbud/napi/issues/8460)

# Deploying

Bookie is automatically deployed to Production when you push to `main` branch.

Therefore, deploying is automatically done for you when you merge a PR. You can track the progress in CircleCI. When it's deployed, you'll receive a Slack notification from the `#releases` channel.

## Deployment workflow

Both preview and production are automatically deployed to GKE with CircleCI.

After all unit and integration tests passed and a docker image is pushed, then we run the following steps:

1. Deploy to bookie preview
2. Run bookie's e2e tests. Note that we don't do this step in CircleCI on working branches, so it is recommended that we run e2e tests ourselves before merging the PR. It would be a faster way at catching regressions.
3. Deploy to production

## Branch deployment

<aside>
⚠️ **Avoid doing this if you can.** Ideally we should do this with a staging app. As we don't currently have it, then we can do it with a preview app (although it isn't recommended). Before doing so, you need to notify the engineering team in case that we disrupt their work.

</aside>

So you want to deploy a working branch to bookie preview, you can do it with terraform:

1. In napi directory, `cd apps/bookie/infrastructure/preview`
2. Make sure that your branch is rebased on main branch.
3. Store the latest commit hash in a variable: `LATEST=${"$(git rev-parse HEAD)":0:9}`
4. `terraform init`
5. `terraform plan -var="commit=$LATEST"`
6. `terraform apply -var="commit=$LATEST"`

It is recommended to use Search API in preview:

The sensitive secrets are stored in [Vault UI](https://vault.busbud-int.com/ui/vault/auth?with=github). The non-sensitive secrets (e.g. feature toggle or public URL) are stored in terraform files in bookie.

# Best Practices

### Ship a migration that deletes data

Such migrations are breaking, because they will remove data that was used by the application. Of course, you have changed the code so it doesn't use this data anymore.

Still, it's better to follow an incremental approach for this:

1. Ship a change that will make the application stop using the data (= you deprecate the data)
2. If everything is fine, ship another change that will effectively remove the data

This is a great approach because it guarantees that each deployment is backward compatible. If something goes wrong with the second deployment and data is gone, we can safely rollback because the code was not using the data anyway!

# Debugging

There are a lot of debugging tools at our disposal and it takes time to know when or how to use them. This page is meant to guide you on which would be appropriate debugging tool to use.

## Sentry

We use [Sentry](https://sentry.io/organizations/busbudcom/issues/?project=97764) to track errors, to know things that should not happen and exceptions that we need to act on. Ideally, we should have no error here.

It's usually the quickest way to know if a regression was introduced after a production deployment.

## Datadog

We use Datadog for monitoring, to see how our systems are performing by sending relevent events to generate useful graphs and alerts.

You'll find monitoring for fraud, payment success rate, cart creation success rate, and more.

[Bookie monitor](https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/itd-hk4-s3r/bookie?from_ts=1642087412905&to_ts=1642088312905&live=true)

[Payments squad monitors](https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/lists/manual/17323)

### APM

We use APM in Datadog for performance monitoring, to check latency for both bookie app and databases.

APM for bookie is linked [here](https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/service/bookie/express.request?env=production&topGraphs=latency%3Alatency%2CbreakdownAs%3Apercentage%2Cerrors%3Aversion_count%2Chits%3Aversion_count&start=1642086736759&end=1642090336759&paused=false).

APM for bookie database is linked [here](https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/service/bookie-postgres/pg.query?env=production&topGraphs=latency%3Alatency%2Cerrors%3Acount%2Chits%3Acount&start=1642086799485&end=1642090399485&paused=false).

## Support Tool

It's an [application](https://support.busbud-int.com/) used by CX to manage the purchases. There's plenty of information about each purchase, which can be useful to debug an issue. It's usually a good tool to start with before using the logs.

## Logs

### When to use it?

For anything.  Most endpoints, workers, cron jobs and application services are being logged. It is typically used after Sentry or Datadog where you'd know that something is going on in production.

If you're trying to figure out what's going in production and you're missing information, then adding new logs would be a good approach to do.

### Where to find them?

Bookie's logs are saved in Google Cloud Storage (GCS). We use `@busbud/busbud-logger` to store our logs. This is a package developed by the Supply squad.

Our logs are uploaded to Google Cloud Storage. You can access them using `bb gcs-logs`.

Once connected on the machine, move to the Bookie folder:

```
cd ../gcs-mounts/busbud_logs/bookie/

```

Here, logs are stored inside folders by date. Inside each folder, logs are stored in files by UTC hour.

You can then `cat`/`grep`/`ack`/`jq` the hell out of it to find what you're looking for. It can be really useful to gather more details than what we send to Sentry or Datadog.

## Database

In addition to bookie database, we also have the following:

### Redis

We mainly use it to look up a cart. Since all carts are encoded before being persisted, there's a [script](https://github.com/busbud/napi/blob/661a94655c023f4c2e18e8accb3add00d37c2bb0/apps/bookie/scripts/debug-tools/cart-lookup.ts#L23) in bookie to make it easier to decode a cart.

### Big Query

Big Query stores a lot of things, but what we care about as a payments squad is that it stores all information about a user's event path in pubweb. It could be helpful when Amplitude isn't enough.

You'd need a user's cookie to be able to look them up. If you have one of their purchases, then you can use a purchase ID to get the cookie:

```sql
SELECT
timestamp
, response_time
, content_length
, status
, cookie_H
, cookie_S
, referrer
, url
FROM
  `departure-archive.fastly_logs_mtl.logs_prod_pubweb`
WHERE
  DATE(timestamp) BETWEEN "2021-10-22"
  AND "2021-10-23"
  AND url like '%/PURCHASE_ID%' order by timestamp desc;
```

Cookie definitions:

```
cookie_H: identify the user (saved for two years)
cookie_S: identify the session
cookie_U: identify the currency (customer's preferences)
cookie_N: identify napi token
cookie_X: identify the XP
```

Once you extract `cookie_H`, then you can use it to look up all of a user's activities (e.g. URL visited, API endpoints called, etc...)

### ADB (Analytics database)

Used by marketing and product teams for analytics and reporting. Bookie exports its data to ADB.

# Flex

[https://github.com/busbud/flex](https://github.com/busbud/flex)

## Overview

Flex handles serving city, location, and route information to its consumers. Flex is responsible for:

1. Serving autocomplete suggestions for the search form on the website
2. Resolving routes for a given origin/destination pair
3. Resolving route stats for interconnection

Flex runs behind Fastly in order to optimize request latency.

### Serving autocomplete suggestions

The suggestions endpoint takes a query as a parameter and returns a list of suggestions. For example, if a user types `mont` in the search form, it is Flex’s responsibility to return a list of suggestions that are relevant based on user’s location and input. In this case, suggestions such as `Montreal, Canada` and `Monterrey, Mexico` will be returned by Flex.

One thing to note is that a suggestion can be either a city or location. It makes use of the `places` table in Flex’s DB, which is a union of the `cities` and `locations` table in Grand Central.

### Resolving routes

Once an origin and destination have been selected, the routes endpoint provides a list of route matches for a given origin/destination pair.
