# Inventory Service

[https://github.com/busbud/inventory-service](https://github.com/busbud/inventory-service)

## Overview

Inventory Service communicates with the suppliers’ adapters to fetch departures and save the responses from the adapters to its cache. It also decides whether fresh departures should be fetched from suppliers based on caching policies. It is composed of a main process and two workers (`Search Worker`, `Cache Writer`). On a high level, Inventory Service is responsible for:

1. Querying cached departures
2. Fetching departures from suppliers
    1. Sends a request to the supplier using the supplier’s adapter
    2. Waits for the adapter’s response with supplier data
3. Writing departures to cache
4. Making refresh decisions based caching policies

### Querying cached departures

Once Inventory Service receives a `SearchInfo` from Poll Service, it first looks in the cache (Redis) to see if there are cached departures. If it is a cache hit, the cached departures are sent to Poll Service. At the same time, Inventory Service evaluates whether it should refresh the cached departures by initiating a new search to the supplier based on caching policies which will be discussed in detail below. If it is a cache miss, Inventory Service initiates a new search to the supplier.

A debouncer is used to prevent triggering multiple requests for identical `SearchInfos` if they are requested at the same time. Redis is used to keep track of active searches. If a search is already initiated for a given `SearchInfo`, the debouncer will skip sending the search event to Search Worker.

### Fetching departures from suppliers

The main process delegates the fetching task to Search Worker. The sole responsibility of a Search Worker is to send the request to the supplier’s adapter and hand off the response to Cache Writer.

### Writing departures to cache

Cache Writer saves the new departures it received from Search Worker to cache. It also updates cache if there are errors while connecting to the supplier or during the purchase flow. These errors are later used by caching policies to determine whether cached departures for a given `SearchInfo` should be refreshed.

### Making refresh decisions based caching policies

For every `SearchInfo` it receives, Inventory Service assesses whether it should refresh cache or not based on caching policies. Each caching policy has a scoring algorithm to give a score based on the given search context. The sum of all applicable policy scores is then normalized using a sigmoid function (policies can be applied/skipped based on the search context). Finally, the normalized score is compared with a random number and if the score is greater than the random number, the cache entry is refreshed. Assuming that the normalized score range is from 0 to 1, a normalized score of 0.7 will have a 70% chance of refreshing.

Example policies:

- If the age of the cache is old, return a high score
- If time to departure is small, return a high score
- If available seats are low, return a high score
- If a booking error has been associated with any of the departures, return a high score
- If a price change has been associated with any of the departures, return a high score

# Mapping-Service

## Overview

 https://github.com/busbud/mapping-service

Mapping Service is responsible for automatically mapping our sources’ x-mappings to Busbud locations and cities, allowing them to be displayed on the website without the need for manual human interference.

Due to the complex nature of interpreting the data we receive from partners, the service holds many source-specific configurations and restrictions, which lives in hardcoded files scattered throughout the service.

Alongside, the service has its own database, that holds the allowed bots per source.

## The Mappers

Note: The following details are written in the perspective of a source who’s configuration allows for the specified mapper to be run.

### Radius Mapper

(This is the first mapper to be run before all the other mappers when configured.)

The Radius Mapper is run on all x-mappings for a source that have a lat/lon with at least 4 decimal points of precision. It will compare this lat/lon with our database of locations, and find the closest good location that is within 30 meters. 

When a match is not found, the x-mapping is not mapped.

This is intuitively our most successful mapper, as it looks for an existing, approved Busbud location that is at most a 2-minute walk away.

This mapper should not be run for:

- Any sources where we use hodor tickets, and rely on the exact description of the location and its address to guide the user to the correct boarding location

### Locations And Cities Creator Mapper

Technical README: https://github.com/busbud/mapping-service/blob/master/src/mappers/locations-creator-mapper/README.md

The Locations-and-cities Creator Mapper (referenced as just the “locations creator” below for length reasons) leverages the lat/lon of each x-mapping to ask Google for a proper location and city.

In essence, it:

- gives google a lat/lon, asks google what the location and city are
- looks for a matching location in our Busbud database. If it finds one based on Google’s returned lat/lon, then we assign the x-mapping that location, and we are done. Otherwise continue on
- looks for a matching city in our Busbud database
    - if it doesn’t find one, it creates one (city-creator portion)
- after the city is created, it creates a location, assigns the location to the city as well as the xmapping
- There are many points in the flow that can cause a mapping attempt to be discarded. These are logged into the engineering log box, while the final result is posted on the #integration-imports slack channel

Common sources of issues:

- TL;DR: heavy reliance on google working like we expect it to
- When we create a new location, we can either rely on the name from the google result, or the original name of our x-mapping. We default to the Google name unless specified otherwise
    - We can specify “otherwise” in our database config. For example, all our betterez sources rely on the x-mapping name for the location name
    - Sometimes we can rely on the x-mapping name after some form of systemic clean up. This logic is hardcoded [here](https://github.com/busbud/mapping-service/blob/master/src/mappers/locations-creator-mapper/configs/location-creator-sources.ts)
- While Busbud has simple logic of “a city is associated with a state/province/region, which is then associated to a country”, that’s not how a lot of the world works. Google doesn’t return a “city”, “state” nor “country”, it returns `administrative district 1`, `administrative district 2`, `administrative district 3`, 4… etc, based on how many nested administrative districts a country can have. Because of this, for every country, we have to manually connect which values we need to get our city and region values. These are hardcoded [here](https://github.com/busbud/mapping-service/blob/master/src/mappers/city-creator/configs/city-creator-countries.ts#L39). **Any country not in this list is not eligible for city creation.**
- Associated with the above, a google region might not have the same spelling or locale of that in our database, not to mention naming changes in the ongoing years. In order to match to the correct region, we have a hardcoded configuration folder that lists which google region is which Busbud region [here](https://github.com/busbud/mapping-service/tree/master/src/mappers/city-creator/configs/countries)
    - As such, any google region name that is not found within this list will be ignored, and the x-mapping not mapped

### Low-Details Mapper

Technical README: https://github.com/busbud/mapping-service/blob/master/src/mappers/low-details-mapper/README.md

NOTE: at the time of writing, this mapper has been disabled for all sources due to the low success rate, and anecdotally causing more harm than good

The Low-Details mapper attempts to map x-mappings to city centers when x-mappings don’t have a lat/lon. Instead, it relies *purely* on the x-mapping’s name, queries google and foursquare to find a location on the earth, and maps to it.

When a location is found by google and foursquare, it repeats the process of the locations-creator mapper to create the city and location as needed.

### Station Mapper

The Station Mapper was created when we were notified a small amount of x-mappings for a source had different physical locations depending on the operator operating it. Because of this, we had to split *all* of our x-mappings for that source by operator. However, assuming that the problem is only a small subset of x-mappings, and that most XIDs are only associated with one operator anyways, our manual mappers would be doing a significant excess load of work, and we would be filtering out supply until we map to the exact same location for the operator-specific x-mapping.

The Station Mapper therefore finds all the x-mappings for a source that need mapping, and remaps the x-mappings for a specific operator (typically noted by an operatorID in the xid) and maps them to the exact same location as its “parent” x-mapping that is not denoted with an operatorID.

For example:

- a search with x-mapping XID `1` yields x-mappings `1:operatorA` and `1:operatorB`
- station mapper will map `1:operatorA` and `1:operatorB` to the same location as `1`

Due to the incredibly-specific nature of this mapper, it is the only one that is not controlled by the database configuration, but rather by the hardcoded file of sources to run on [here](https://github.com/busbud/mapping-service/blob/master/src/mappers/station-mapper/station-mapper-sources.ts#L56)

At the time of writing, it is only used for:

- pinbus
- centraldepasajes
- and NOT chilepasajes, due to too many x-mappings having different physical locations

# Other Applications

Busbud is split up into several applications, microservices, and modules. This is a quick over on each application, how the Core Squad will find themselves using them, and how each is connected to one another. Note this list doesn’t contain all of our Node.js modules, you’ll find the larger list in the [integrations docs](busbud-modules.md).

## Integration

An integration is the source of our inventory on Busbud.com. It’s a microservice that queries and converts data from inventory partners API’s to Busbud’s standards.

### Adapter

An adapter consists of mainly two files which you can learn about in [integrations](../integration/integrations.md), `api.ts` for communication to the partners API, and `index.ts` for converting data to Busbud’s standard. See [integrations](../integration/integrations.md) for a more in-depth explanation.

### BELa

[BELa](https://github.com/busbud/integration-bela) is the HTTP layer that sits on top of an adapter. It handles creating [express](https://expressjs.com/) endpoints that are passed along to each individual adapter method. Whenever an external service communicates to an adapter, all requests pass through BELa first before reaching the adapter method. BELa also handles things such as authentication, tracking, and error reporting. You can see an example of a live integration with BELa on the [Transcor](https://int-transcor.busbud-int.com/) integration, and seeing available endpoints for a source on the integration by appending the source to the end of the URL, e.g. [BlackHills](https://int-transcor.busbud-int.com/blackhills).

Configuration for BELa is handled by the [integration framework](https://github.com/busbud/integration-framework) which you can read about in the [modules docs](busbud-modules.md#int).

## NAPI

[NAPI](https://github.com/busbud/napi) is the main consumer of Integrations. It’s the core API of Busbud that sits in-between the integrations and all its client’s such as Busbud.com, the mobile apps, and our internal tools such as Busplatform and Support Tool (which you’ll read about later). Napi is split up in to three services, Grand Central, Bookie ,and Il-controllore. Each of these services have a production environment for the public, and a preview environment used for internal testing.

### Grand Central

[Grand Central](https://github.com/busbud/napi/tree/master/apps/grand-central) handles all the schedule search calls for its clients. It also implements a cache in order to reduce calls to the integrations, and in turn reduce load on our partners. Everything that falls under the `search` flow is handled by Grand Central.

### Bookie

[Bookie](https://github.com/busbud/napi/tree/master/apps/bookie) handles all the booking and purchase calls for its clients. Everything that falls under the `booking` flow is handled by Bookie.

### Il-controllore

[Il-controllore](https://github.com/busbud/napi/tree/master/apps/il-controllore) is the authentication service for nearly all of the services across Busbud, including integrations, Napi, Importer, Dora, etc. Il-controllore wasn’t always the at the center of authentication however, you can read more about the history in the [integration changelog](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/tree/master/_changelog).

## Importer

The [importer](https://github.com/busbud/integration-importer) is a microservice that sits in-between the integrations and Napi. Its job is to handle calling the integrations [getLocations](/tsdocs/interfaces/_busbud_int_schemas_schemas_adapter.genericadapter.html#getlocations) and [getRoutes](/tsdocs/interfaces/_busbud_int_schemas_schemas_adapter.genericadapter.html#getroutes) methods on a daily basis to import new locations and routes from our partners, and keeping a cache in its own database returning only the new/changed locations and routes to Napi, minimizing the load on Napi’s database.

In Napi you’ll find `locations` from the importer are saved in the `x_mappings`, and `routes` saved in `x_routes`.

## Backoffice

[Backoffice](https://backoffice.busbud-int.com/dashboard) is the all-in-one internal tool for managing information on Busbud.com. One of the big tasks it has is making it easy to map the locations returned from the integrations [getLocations](/tsdocs/interfaces/_busbud_int_schemas_schemas_adapter.genericadapter.html#getlocations) to cities and stops searchable on Busbud.com. Busplatform communications directly with Napi in order to retrieve and save mapping information after it’s been returned from the importer.

## Dora

[Dora](https://github.com/busbud/dora) is a routes discovery service for the integrations. Sometimes partners provide minimal or no routes at all that can be imported through [getRoutes](/tsdocs/interfaces/_busbud_int_schemas_schemas_adapter.genericadapter.html#getroutes). Dora has [multiple strategies](https://github.com/busbud/dora#strategies) in which it takes list of locations provided by [getLocations](/tsdocs/interfaces/_busbud_int_schemas_schemas_adapter.genericadapter.html#getlocations) and do searches against the integration to see if results are returned. Once results are found, the route is submitted to the importer to be added to daily imports to Napi.

## Pubweb

[Pubweb](https://github.com/busbud/public-website) is the frontend React application that runs Busbud.com. Core squad mainly uses Pubweb’s preview environment for debugging and testing.

## Hodor

[Hodor](https://github.com/busbud/hodor) is a PDF generation microservice. It handles generating tickets for integrations that do not have a `getTickets` method. It also has the capabilities for taking an HTML response from a partners API and converting it to a PDF, which for example is done for the [Central De Pasajes](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/5e354536f0235622cc860f8359173553c2904a69/centraldepasajes/src/adapter/api.js#L290) integration.

## Support Tool

[Support Tool](https://github.com/busbud/busbud-support) is the main application used by the Customer Experience team for managing purchases. It can be a useful tool for find and beginning to debug purchase issues for an integration.

## Sherlock

[Sherlock](https://github.com/busbud/sherlock) is used to run [BATS](https://github.com/busbud/busbud-adapter-testsuite) over production logs, looking for errors that were missed or not present during an integrations development. This allows to quickly find issues in production before they’re reported by other people/services.

## Overseer

[Overseer](https://github.com/busbud/busbud-overseer) is a microservice designed to run cron job styled tasks related to alerting and reporting. Core squad mainly uses this service to report [booking errors](https://github.com/busbud/busbud-overseer/blob/master/tasks/booking-failures.js) to Flowdock and Pagerduty/OpsGenie.

## Logger Service

[Logger Service](https://github.com/busbud/integration-logger-service) handles consuming logs from the integrations and any other services using [`busbud-logger`](https://github.com/busbud/busbud-logger), and saving them to Google Cloud Storage. Logs are submitted to the logger service by POST requests with [busbud-logger](https://github.com/busbud/busbud-logger), making consumption easy, and allows us not to be vendor locked to any specific infrastructure or framework.

# ADRs

# Intro: why

Architecture decision records (ADRs) are crucial for setting the long-term vision of a code base, especially when considering refactors that cannot be easily encapsulated within a single issue.

They provide essential context and reasoning behind decisions that might not be immediately obvious or trivial at a first glance. By documenting these decisions, teams can ensure that the rationale behind architectural choices is clear and can be revisited and understood by current and future team members. Furthermore, ADRs can include experiments or ideas we tried that didn't work out. These give us useful lessons for making better decisions in the future.

This not only helps in maintaining a coherent and consistent architecture but also facilitates smoother collaboration and decision-making processes over time.

# 1. Use Domain Models (2024-02-20)

## Context

Poll-service orchestrates the retrieval, contextualization, and aggregation of trips sourced from inventory-service. Aside from the contextualization models that come from GC, poll-service used to work with two different types: `Trip` and `PublicTrip`.

- `Trip` was the UDM trip model defined by the integration.
- `PublicTrip` was contextualized version of the trip that was later exposed to clients.

Given that trip types may evolve over time, it's imperative to mitigate the risk of cascading refactors that could arise from changes in the Adapter and poll-service's public  types, as we've seen with the arrival of Classes & Fares.

Additionally we can't expect our clients to evolve at the same pace, it is certain that we are going to be in a situation where we have to consume adapter trips at the latest version and return public trips of an older version.

## Decision

We will use domain models to represent the core business entities and encapsulate the business logic, decoupling them from the API types. This approach allows us to maintain a single codebase while accommodating the evolving needs of different client applications, whether they require compatibility with legacy API versions or demand access to the latest features and functionalities.

In concrete:

- `DomainTrip` is the domain model for the trip and it represents contextualized and possibly aggregated trips (interconnections / fake roundtrips).
- `AdapterTrip` is the trip returned by inventory-service which should be used only for contextualization or pre contextualization validation
- `PublicTrip` is the trip exposed through the API which naturally is going to hold a subset of `DomainTrip` 's information.
- Business logic is applied to `DomainTrip`s (filtering, aggregation, annotations).
- Business logic is applied seamlessly to one ways or aggregated trips
- Trip fetching is encapsulated trough repositories whose implementation can be replaced. For example, we should aim to have the ability of adding a L1 cache for contextualized trips without changes in application or domain services

## Consequences

This approach allows us to maintain a single codebase for all trip types while accommodating the evolving needs of different client applications, whether they require compatibility with legacy API versions or demand access to the latest features and functionalities.

# 2. New folder structure for routes (2024-02-20)

## Context

Our application needs to support multiple versions of APIs to accommodate evolving requirements and ensure backward compatibility. Currently, our folder structure is not optimized for managing different API versions, leading to potential confusion and inefficiencies in development and maintenance.

## Decision

We have decided to reorganize our folder structure to better support multiple API versions. Specifically, we will introduce version-specific subdirectories under the `presentation` directory, where express controllers reside. Each version-specific subdirectory (`v3`, `v4`, etc.) will contain response formatters tailored to the respective API version. However, the core business logic and services, located in the `service` directory, will remain version-agnostic. This separation allows us to isolate version-specific changes and additions, making it easier to manage and maintain the codebase.

```ruby
src/components/search/application/
├── presentation
│   ├── get-trip-handler.ts # Parse request, call use case, format response
│   ├── v3
│   │   ├── trip-details-response-formatter.ts
│   └── v4
│       ├── trip-details-response-formatter.ts
└── service
    ├── get-trip-by-id.ts # Use case, returns domain models
```

See this in action [here](https://github.com/busbud/poll-service/blob/c3061cc54b53ba96b908965dc519477617055d8c/src/routes/routes.ts#L709-L726)

## Consequences

- **Improved Organization:** The new folder structure provides a clear separation between different API versions, enhancing code organization and maintainability.
- **Smoother Upgrades:** Developers can easily identify and modify version-specific code without affecting other versions or the core business logic.
- **Enhanced Scalability:** The modular approach enables us to add support for new API versions more efficiently, reducing development time and effort.
- **Potential Overhead:** Managing multiple versions may introduce additional overhead in terms of code review, testing, and documentation. However, the benefits of improved organization and scalability outweigh this potential drawback.

# 3. Use Object Mother pattern for integration tests (2024-02-20)

## Context

In the process of designing tests for the PS project, the complexity of setting up test scenarios, particularly those involving the contextualization of trips, has become apparent. The multitude of models and their interrelationships present a significant challenge in creating comprehensive and efficient test setups. While the preference is typically to maintain explicitness within test blocks, the effort required for setting up contextualized trip tests is substantial.

## **Decision**

We propose the adoption of the Object Mother pattern to streamline the setup of integration tests, specifically focusing on contextualization scenarios. The Object Mother pattern involves defining a static repository of real-world locations, cities, sources, classes, and other relevant entities, which serve as a foundation for generating test cases.

See it in action [here](https://github.com/busbud/poll-service/blob/c3061cc54b53ba96b908965dc519477617055d8c/src/components/search/application/service/get-trip-by-id.integration.test.ts#L108-L141)

### **Rationale**

1. **Reduced Setup Complexity**: The Object Mother pattern significantly reduces the complexity of setting up integration tests by providing a pre-defined universe of relevant entities. This alleviates the burden of manually creating and configuring numerous test scenarios.
2. **Improved Maintainability**: By centralizing the definition of test data within the Object Mother repository, maintenance becomes more straightforward. Changes or updates to the test data can be made in one location, ensuring consistency across all relevant test cases.
3. **Enhanced Test Focus**: With the Object Mother pattern handling the setup of contextualized trips, testers can focus more on verifying the behavior and interactions of the system under test, rather than spending excessive time on data setup.

### **Considerations**

1. **Coupling Concerns**: While the Object Mother pattern offers significant benefits, there is a risk of introducing tight coupling between tests and the test data repository. To mitigate this, the use of the Object Mother pattern will be restricted to contextualization scenarios only.

### **Implementation Details**

1. **Refactoring for Separation**: As part of ongoing refactoring efforts, we will aim to separate the contextualization logic from other aspects of the system. This separation will ensure that contextualization, including the use of the Object Mother pattern, remains isolated and easily maintainable.
2. **Limited Scope**: The Object Mother pattern will be applied exclusively to integration tests and the transformation between adapter trips and domain models. Other aspects of testing will continue to utilize regular domain model factories, which are already contextualized.

## **Conclusion**

The adoption of the Object Mother pattern for integration tests, focusing on contextualization scenarios, offers significant advantages in terms of reducing setup complexity, improving maintainability, and enhancing test focus. By carefully restricting its use and integrating it into ongoing refactoring efforts, we can harness its benefits while mitigating potential drawbacks.

# 3. Handling Multiple Fares for Price Groups with Multiple Operators

## Context

We have a business rule that stipulates that a trip can only have one fare per price group. This rule ensures that segments within an adapter trip are booked together under the same terms and conditions. However, we encounter scenarios where a price group contains multiple operators with different fares, making it challenging to adhere to this rule.

## Decision

After exploring various solutions, we have decided on the following approach to handle cases where a price group contains multiple operators with different fares:

1. **Use the source’s fare when available :** In situations where one of the operators doesn’t have a fare override, we will prioritize using the fare provided by the source associated with that operator.
2. **Use the first operator's fare if all operators have fare overrides:** If all operators have fare overrides, we will default to using the fare associated with the first operator. This is because fares in the search context are indexed by operator

**Rationale:**

We think that the described approach is a good trade off  because it's easy to implement and it can be worked around by having the integration return a special fare for trips with multiple operators and use that as an override.

**Alternatives Considered:**

- **Use the more restrictive fare:** This approach was deemed impractical due to the multidimensional nature of fares, where one fare might be more restrictive in some aspects but more flexible in others.
- **Merge fares together:** While conceptually appropriate, merging fares adds complexity and risk to the existing terms model

# Poll Service

[https://github.com/busbud/poll-service](https://github.com/busbud/poll-service)

[ADRs](Poll Service/ADRs.md)

## Overview

Poll Service is responsible for gathering data for a given search and assembling the data in order to serve users with departures. Poll Service achieves this by delegating tasks to both Flex (for retrieving routes) and Inventory Service (for retrieving departures). As the name suggests, Poll Service is polled by the client until all departures are served. Once users initiate a search, Poll Service is responsible for:

1. Retrieving routes for a given origin/destination pair from Flex
2. Retrieving departures for each route from Inventory Service
3. Assembling the departures and serving them to users
4. Handling polling from the client

### Retrieving routes from Flex

Flex returns a list of routes that are composed of `source_id`, `origin_xid`, and `destination_xid`. Poll Service decorates each route with additional context such as `outbound_date` and `return_date` and `passenger_counts`. The combination of route, date, and passenger_counts is called a `SearchInfo`. It is used as an input for Inventory Service, which is responsible for fetching departures from suppliers and caching them.

### Retrieving departures from Inventory Service

Poll Service sends requests to Inventory Service for each `SearchInfo` in order to retrieve departures. If Inventory Service has cached departures for a given `SearchInfo`, it will return the cached departures. If not, Inventory Service will fetch departures through the supplier’s adapters in the background. While Inventory Service waits to get fresh departures and populate them in cache, Poll Service assembles the departures it received from Inventory Service for that poll before returning them to the client. Poll Service is polled until departures for every `SearchInfo` has been served to the client.

### Assembling the departures

(In progress) The assembling part is currently handled by Grand Central (`process-departures`). We are in the middle of migrating it over to Poll Service.

### Handling polling from the client

Poll Service keeps track of the poll state using Redis. Keyed by the `request_id`, the poll state keeps track of whether departures have been returned for each route. Polling will continue until the state of each route is marked as “complete”.

# SLOs

# Introduction

## Goals

- Hold our core services to a **high standard** of response time and success rate to ensure user satisfaction.
- Create a **scalable** alerting system based on high-level patterns rather than individual pain points
- Establish alerts based on metrics that are **as close to and relevant for the user** as possible
- Take a **standardized, consistent, documented** approach to defining acceptable performance
- Maintain **product velocity** while ensuring show-stopping bugs do not go uncorrected
- To promote a **healthy culture** of engineering with reliability in mind, accountability without shaming when things go wrong
- Remember the main point of alerts: to notify an engineer of a problem that requires **immediate manual intervention or notification to correct or mitigate**.

## Terminology

- **Service Level Indicators** (**SLIs**) are the metrics used to measure the level of service provided to end users (e.g., availability, latency, throughput).
- **Service Level Objectives** (**SLOs**) are the targeted levels of service, measured by SLIs. They are typically expressed as a percentage over a period of time.
- **Service Level Agreements** (**SLAs**) are contractual agreements that outline the level of service end users can expect from service providers. If these promises are not met, there can be significant consequences for the provider, which are often financial in nature (e.g., service credits, subscription extensions).
- **Error budgets** are the acceptable levels of unreliability for a service before it falls out of compliance with an SLO. Simply put, they are the difference between 100 percent reliability and the SLO target. You can think of error budgets like financial budgets—except in this case, developers spend their budgets on building out new features, redesigning system architectures, or any other product development work.

*(Source: [https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/establishing-service-level-objectives/](https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/establishing-service-level-objectives/))*

# Appendix

## Integration Tier Definitions

All definitions are based on a rolling average of daily sales taken across the last 31 days.

- **Tier 1:** integrations selling more than 400 tickets per day OR $1000 per day in revenue
- **Tier 2:** integrations selling more than 100 tickets per day OR $300 per day in revenue
- **Tier 3:** integrations selling more than 50 tickets per day OR $100 per day in revenue
- **Tier 4:** integrations selling more than 10 tickets per day OR $30 per day in revenue
- **Tier 5:** integrations selling at least 1 ticket per day OR $5 per day in revenue (virtually inactive)

# ADO

## ❓API requests failing due to “Usuario, Estación o Punto de Venta no autorizado” or 500 internal errors

ADO has a bug in their system where one to many of the process’ in their node pools will start failing auth requests, or throw 500 errors. This happens randomly without any changes being made from us or ADO.

To solve the issue, ADO must reboot their services. The following screenshot is from one of their Engineerings/PMs on July 24th, 2024 explaining how he fixed the issue.

![Untitled](ADO/Untitled.png)

Another from October 4th, 2024

![Screenshot 2024-10-04 at 1.42.48 PM.png](ADO/Screenshot_2024-10-04_at_1.42.48_PM.png)

# Betterez (any)

## ❓No API Cancellation?

Source currency (on backoffice) has to have to same currency as our betterez account-configured currency in order for API cancellation to be permitted.

We currently have betterez accounts in the following currencies:

- CAD
- USD
- MXN
- ARS

Note that if the source is significantly old (before Betterez joined Busbud), the source might still be on the USD betterez account, while sporting a different source currency on backoffice.

If unusure, feel free to reach out to rocket, who can check the credentials of the source vs the `default_source_config_${currency}` configurations we have stored in vault.

# Distribusion

# Operator notes

## SRAI (Slovak Rail)

**Frequent Price Inconsistency**

Distribusion advised that they have poor rate limiting with the operator SRAI on their side, which results in many outdated search results. Distribusion is working on improving the stats, so it is out of our control.

Example: 

Price response on `GET /retailers/v4/connections/find` ([link](https://gist.github.com/svetlana-br/374d2429619f5413112b183e834693db#file-01-L63)) differs from price received on `GET /retailers/v4/connections/vacancy` ([link](https://gist.github.com/svetlana-br/374d2429619f5413112b183e834693db#file-04-L32))

# Movelia

## ❓No seat selection on Alsa

Alsa’s seat selection is per-selection with free default seats. With our current product, it’d only lead to more confusion for the average user. There is currently [a bet](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1gJ7LkclWdqIuojz9lQeG-OjSTKBlec-0Im1Yb0GqD4s/edit#heading=h.oy289bik04c4) for supporting this.

## ❓No seat selection on non-Alsa

1. They might have the same issue as alsa
2. Some movelia operators don’t give us seat selection. Please confirm behaviour on movelia’s website before bringing it forward to engineering or supplyQA

## ❓Why are RedeExpressos buses flagged as Alsa?

Our contract deals state that buses from Portugal → Spain are advertised as RedeExpressos, while buses Spain → Portugal are advertised as Alsa, regardless of what their own websites say.

As such, our redeexpressos source only serves Portugal → Spain, while movelia serves Spain → Portugal

# Pinbus

### Flota Occidental returning the wrong layout

We’ve previously been flagged that we are returning the wrong layout for Flota Occidental.

Here’s the slack thread: https://busbud.slack.com/archives/CDLHQFT9V/p1761659920893479

At the time of writing, Pinbus is investigating the issue here: https://busbud.slack.com/archives/C01U54PK4PL/p1761666090989639

# Raileurope

## ❓Supply not showing up

Come back after SNCF is moved off. We have strict rate limits we need to abide by (due to SNCF) so coverage is not optimal.

## ❓Child/Senior fares not displaying discounted price

Our integration is still on the old model, where we can’t take advantage of the ages of our customers. We’d need a full raileurope rewrite, which is currently not in the works.

## ❓Why does Renfe have so many passenger questions?

We parse passenger questions based on what the raileurope API says we need to answer. So for Renfe on raileurope, they are required.

## ❓Passenger Booked an interconnection but only got one ticket

Fast fix: On the support tool purchase page, open up the “Departure” section of the Departure Details section and do a CMD+F for “ticket_urls”. All the ticketURLs are there

Eventual fix (or just a rewrite): 

[https://github.com/busbud/integrations/issues/10113](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/issues/10113)

# Ratality (any)

## ❓Why is it asking for gender? No one asks for gender

Yes they do. Under the guise of choosing the title “Mr” or “Mrs”.

# Rede Expressos

## ❓Transfer is not shown

This is because Rede Expressos’ backend does not specify to us the transfer information. 

We do return an `unknown transfer count` that shows the number of transfers, but we don’t know where they are. This parameter has not been adopted by clients like pubweb and mobile.

## ❓Why are Alsa buses flagged as RedeExpressos?

Our contract deals state that buses from Portugal → Spain are advertised as RedeExpressos, while buses Spain → Portugal are advertised as Alsa, regardless of what their own websites say.

As such, our redeexpressos source only serves Portugal → Spain, while movelia serves Spain → Portugal

###

# Sprinterbus / Vamoose / Bestbus

## ❓Not showing up on Mobile

These guys are all Spreedly, PMD integrations. While mobile does not support

# Tickets Bolivia

## ❓The trip duration is abnormally short/long

TicketsBolivia doesn’t give us an arrival time, nor an arrival stop (only an arrival *city*). Therefore the duration you see on Busbud is estimated via the geolocations of the origin and destination. You can ask supplyQA to make sure the mappings are in the correct city, but otherwise we can’t fix it.

# The Book Of Supply Red Tape (BETA)

*This book is dedicated to all those hours multiple platform members spent answering the same repeated questions about certain supply*

## 🤔 The Supply FAQ~

This page is dedicated to answering frequently asked questions about supply problems on select sources. These will be about their inherent behaviours, and not to be confused with a question to go on SupplyQA about a single route missing supply.

This is for:

- people asking the questions
- Rocket shift answering the questions

You can sift through the source subpages to see if your question already has an answer.

# Adapters Revamp

| Reviewer | Status | Date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| @Jacob Cook  | ✅ Approved | March 12, 2025  |
| @Rodrigo Alanis  | ✅ Approved | March 13, 2025  |
| @Lisa Zhao  | ✅ Approved | 2025-03-13 |
|  |  | March 10, 2025  |
| @Muhammad Aqsam  | ✅ Approved | April 7, 2025  |

## Changelog

- `2025-03-12`: Move `pnpm` from *nice-to-have* to required
- `2025-03-12`: Add section on **Template Engine**
- `2025-03-13`: Add Section on Testgen and Scratch File
- `2025-03-14`: Add info on `util` services, with an example
- `2025-03-14`: Rename `Extended<Model>` to `UDMDetailed<Model>`
- `2025-03-26`: Add `Adapter Test Suite` section

# Introduction

Adapters have been used to create a bridge between Busbud services and partners APIs. Over the years, we had some updates to improve maintainability and reliability as well as to add new features. We moved from JavaScript to Typescript; and then moved from what we call legacy adapters to UDM adapters. But, the boilerplate templates have stayed the same.

This spec proposes the next steps on how to improve adapters.

# Motivation

In recent adapters, we started trying different patterns to try to improve readability, reliability and maintainability. But this means we always spend some time tweaking the code after running the starterpack - since the boilerplate doesn’t have everything we need.

We want to be able to start coding an adapter faster after running the starterpack by including some of the common code/patterns into the generated boilerplate. We also want to use common patterns among all new adapters but without over-engineering them - since adapters have well defined and limited responsibilities.

## Goals

- Have a well defined template for new adapters to be generated via scripts
- Use NX to generate new adapters and generate methods/endpoints

# Proposed Solution

## Overview

The proposed solution is based on the vertical slice pattern. It focuses on what adapters do, and tries to add modularity on top of that.

At a really high level, adapters communicate with a partner API, perform some manipulations and return UDM objects. They split their responsibilities into `flows` (import, search, book and post-purchase) and methods (`getLocations`, `getRoutes`, `getTrips`, etc…). They also have a shared way of making requests to the partner API and getting/validating the information.

On this proposal, the code will be split into `core` and `flows`. `core` will host any shared code between flows, and `flows` will have the methods as use cases.

<aside>
💡

**Note**: about the name `flows` vs `features`, I believe that even though `features` make sense in a vertical slice point of view, adapters currently name them `flows`; and this naming is used extensively throughout the stack (on dashboards and other services). So I propose `flows` to make it consistent with the adapter nomenclature; and also familiarize developers who start working with adapters with the nomenclature.

</aside>

Extra logic will be split into `models` and `services`, which will be responsible for any type of data extraction and data manipulation.

## Models

Models represent a partner’s entity and are responsible for knowing all the context on how to get the information. For example, how to get the segment XID; how to get a DateTime object from the incoming partner trip object or how to check if the trip is available.

This will be created manually, as they depend on each partner API.

![Example: on [Tornadobus](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/d3c677cef63fbb7103ca7c1a68ba6efcd2d91b67/tornadobus/src/flows/search/models/bus-seat.ts#L29-L51), the seat model has logic to extract the cell type](Adapters%20Revamp/image.png)

Example: on [Tornadobus](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/d3c677cef63fbb7103ca7c1a68ba6efcd2d91b67/tornadobus/src/flows/search/models/bus-seat.ts#L29-L51), the seat model has logic to extract the cell type

## Services

Services use models to apply business logic and transform the partner entity into an UDM model to be returned by the adapter.

Services can also be used to handle smaller functions that usually live on `utils.ts`. The idea is to have a way of organizing any utility functions, or transformation functions that can be easily tested. One good example is how TornadoBus has a service for splitting roundtrips:

![[https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/b97791006ac52c4b86c44525d566f662abd21b73/tornadobus/src/core/services/split-roundtrip.ts](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/b97791006ac52c4b86c44525d566f662abd21b73/tornadobus/src/core/services/split-roundtrip.ts)](Adapters%20Revamp/image%201.png)

[https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/b97791006ac52c4b86c44525d566f662abd21b73/tornadobus/src/core/services/split-roundtrip.ts](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/b97791006ac52c4b86c44525d566f662abd21b73/tornadobus/src/core/services/split-roundtrip.ts)

Services will be created manually, as they depend on each partner API.

![Example: on [LibraMotors](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/tree/f7531bfdccc03d254ccdbb0b965534be7d1a52ef/libramotors/src/flows/search/service), search has services for mapping the departure model into a UDM trip, and one service to generate the bus layout.](Adapters%20Revamp/image%202.png)

Example: on [LibraMotors](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/tree/f7531bfdccc03d254ccdbb0b965534be7d1a52ef/libramotors/src/flows/search/service), search has services for mapping the departure model into a UDM trip, and one service to generate the bus layout.

## Methods

Methods use clients to load data (make API requests), use this data to instantiate a Model, and then use Services to transform the models into a UDM object.

<aside>
💡

Note: in adapters where the logic is straightforward, we don’t need to rely on `models` and/or `services`. If the logic is simple enough it can live inside of the method. The idea is to not over-engineer adapters when not needed, but enable the models/services pattern to simplify the logic in complex scenarios.

</aside>

This will be created automatically based on the starterpack questions, and be automatically used by the adapter file (more on it below).

![[Example](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/d3c677cef63fbb7103ca7c1a68ba6efcd2d91b67/tornadobus/src/flows/book/release-trip.use-case.ts) of straightforward method](Adapters%20Revamp/image%203.png)

[Example](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/d3c677cef63fbb7103ca7c1a68ba6efcd2d91b67/tornadobus/src/flows/book/release-trip.use-case.ts) of straightforward method

## Models, Services, Flows and Methods Relation

In a straightforward adapter, each flow can have a single file for each method. If a method requires a lot of extra manipulation, it could have its own folder.

Models and Services should live as close as possible to the methods that uses them. So a model/service used only by `getTrips`, could live inside of a `getTrips` folder (if the method has its own folder) or the `search` flow. If this model/service is shared between all methods of the flow, then it should live inside of the flow under `model`/`service`. If it’s shared across multiple flows, then it should live on `core/model`/`core/service`.

![[Example from LibraMotors](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/tree/f7531bfdccc03d254ccdbb0b965534be7d1a52ef/libramotors/src)](Adapters%20Revamp/image%204.png)

[Example from LibraMotors](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/tree/f7531bfdccc03d254ccdbb0b965534be7d1a52ef/libramotors/src)

## Client

The client is the part of the code responsible for making requests to the partner API and validating the responses. It will be similar to the current client with few additions. It should have its own folder on the core folder (since it’s shared between all flows). We’ll add Zod as default to help validate schemas.

It will have an index file with the client (similar to the client we have today), where authentication and, `makeRequest` and a function that validates the Zod schemas are pre-generated. 

![[Example client form Libramotors](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/f7531bfdccc03d254ccdbb0b965534be7d1a52ef/libramotors/src/core/client/libramotors-client.ts#L126)](Adapters%20Revamp/image%205.png)

[Example client form Libramotors](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/f7531bfdccc03d254ccdbb0b965534be7d1a52ef/libramotors/src/core/client/libramotors-client.ts#L126)

Then another file called `endpoints` will also be included to centralize all endpoints used by the adapter. It will have the necessary types to be used by request/response types.

![[Endpoints example](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/f7531bfdccc03d254ccdbb0b965534be7d1a52ef/libramotors/src/core/client/endpoints.ts) ](Adapters%20Revamp/image%206.png)

💡

The endpoint file is helpful when validating which endpoints are in use, based on Rocket or Product requests

</aside>

Then it should have two folders: one for **request** schemas and one for **response** schemas. Each folder should have an index file that exports all schemas and types, as well as one `RequestType`/`ResponseType` that has a different type depending on the endpoint.

These folders will also have files for each of the partner’s entities, with Zod schemas that describe the used properties and Typescript types inferred by Zod.

The Libramotors [client](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/tree/f7531bfdccc03d254ccdbb0b965534be7d1a52ef/libramotors/src/core/client) is a good example of how this will look like:

Libramotors [client](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/tree/f7531bfdccc03d254ccdbb0b965534be7d1a52ef/libramotors/src/core/client)

## Adapter

The main adapter file will be simplified and not be responsible for methods logic anymore. It will be responsible for starting up the adapter, and setting up all methods/services required.

In the case of adapters that rely on startup calls (like Betterez), the startup logic should be here.

It will also be renamed to `adapter.ts`, and move to the root of the `src` folder. The `adapter` folder will be removed.

After running the starterpack, each method on the adapter file should only make a call to the corresponding method use case.

![[Example from Libramotors](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/f7531bfdccc03d254ccdbb0b965534be7d1a52ef/libramotors/src/adapter.ts#L61-L67)](Adapters%20Revamp/image%208.png)

[Example from Libramotors](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/f7531bfdccc03d254ccdbb0b965534be7d1a52ef/libramotors/src/adapter.ts#L61-L67)

There should also be a script on `package.json` that runs the adapter locally as an http service.

## Tests

Adapters should also support unit tests out-of-the box. So `package.json` will be updated with the required packages, and a script to automatically run unit tests when running `yarn test`.

Unit tests can be added anywhere in the adapter `src` code. They should be created on `__tests__` folders that should be close to the service/method/model they are testing. Tests must end in `.test.ts`, and the unit test script will be looking for `.test.ts` files.

Usage of unit tests is not mandatory, as it depends on each use-case and service that we add - and most time this is tested by testgen. But, it should be promoted. To help with that, the adapter template will include a boilerplate test file so that developers are familiar with where unit tests should be, and are incentivized to add some. 

### Testgen

Several adapters rely on different testgen test flows (one per source, one per flow, etc…). To simplify that, the template will update the default scratch file to create tests based on source and flow. More on that below.

![Example on how SQILLS handle new testgen tests: [https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/b97791006ac52c4b86c44525d566f662abd21b73/sqills2/scratch/viarail/scratch.ts#L246](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/b97791006ac52c4b86c44525d566f662abd21b73/sqills2/scratch/viarail/scratch.ts#L246)](Adapters%20Revamp/image%209.png)

Example on how SQILLS handle new testgen tests: [https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/b97791006ac52c4b86c44525d566f662abd21b73/sqills2/scratch/viarail/scratch.ts#L246](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/blob/b97791006ac52c4b86c44525d566f662abd21b73/sqills2/scratch/viarail/scratch.ts#L246)

### Adapter Test Suite

A nice-to-have update is include a new test on the [adapter-test-suite](https://github.com/busbud/integration-packages/blob/75be979a707bbfacba17f5b80927a5b26cd932cc/packages/busbud-adapter-testsuite/src/methods/v2.js#L104-L116) specifically on the Book method (v2 and v4), where we should ensure that information from different passenger tickets (`response[passenger_id].details.tickets[ticket_id].details`) cannot be overwritten. Since Bookie will merge all ticket details for the same passenger into a single details object, we need to add a new test that checks if information is not lost when Bookie merges the details (as it happened [here](https://github.com/busbud/integrations/pull/11099)).

So for example, the following object would fail this test, since both ticket details would be merged into a single one, and the resulting details would be `"reservation_id": "reservation 2"`:

```json
{
 "passenger_id": {
   "tickets": [
     {
       "details": {
         "reservation_id": "reservation 1"
       }
     },
     {
       "details": {
         "reservation_id": "reservation 2"
       }
     },
   ]
 }
}
```

The following example should pass the test, since after merging both details, the `reservation_ids` would be the same.

```json
{
 "passenger_id": {
   "tickets": [
     {
       "details": {
         "reservation_ids": ["reservation 1","reservation 2"]
       }
     },
     {
       "details": {
         "reservation_ids": ["reservation 1","reservation 2"]
       }
     },
   ]
 }
}
```

Note that if they have different properties and can be merged without losing data, the test should not fail. The following example should be valid:

```json
{
 "passenger_id": {
   "tickets": [
     {
       "details": {
         "reservation_ids": ["reservation 1","reservation 2"]
       }
     },
     {
       "details": {}
     },
   ]
 }
}
```

## Scratch File

The scratch files will have a few updates. The implementation details will be decided by the developer who implements the, but the requirements are:

- Allow unused imports/vars by default
- Have test passengers/purchasers on a separate mock file
- Have a default configuration for type of flow
- Have a `test_root_dir` that takes into account the flow type and source name.

## Extended Detailed Models

Currently, all `details` objects (on `segments`, `prices`, `passengers`, `reserveResponse`, etc…) are typed as `[k: string]: any;`.  This means we don’t have type safety when adding extra information on these objects.

Some adapters adopted a pattern of extending UDM types into `Extended<Model>` / `UDM<Model>WithDetails` (`ExtendedTrip` / `UDMTripWithDetails` for example), and using them on all functions across the adapter to ensure type safety (so that we don’t forget to add the data when returning UDM objects, and to make sure we use the correct types when accessing those).

We want to make that a default on new adapters. These models should live in `core/models/UDMDetailed<model>/ts`, and be automatically used by the adapter and each use case method (all methods function signatures should use `UDMDetailedTrip` instead of `UDM.Trip`).

## NX

NX js is a tool that is currently being used in other monorepos and can help us improve usage on the integrations repository.

NX has configurations for running projects, running tests, deploying and generating new projects.

The integrations repository should be configured to use NX. And NX should have scripts for (could be via `package.json`):

- Running the scratch file
- Running the adapter locally
- Running the testgen
- Running unit/testgen tests
- Deploying an adapter
- Adding a new method to an integration
- Adding a new endpoint with request/response templates on a client and a function on the client `index.ts`

<aside>
💡

Note: we should still keep using separate `package.json` files and **NOT** merge all adapters to reuse the same dependencies.

</aside>

### Template Engine

NX has [documentation](https://nx.dev/extending-nx/recipes/creating-files) on how to use generators to create/manipulate files, in which it specifies that [EJS](https://ejs.co/) is used as the template engine.

From the docs, EJS seems powerful enough to handle all scenarios mentioned on this spec. The docs don’t mention using custom templates, but given that there’s a function responsible for generating files and it simply calls `generateFiles` , we could easily modify it an use any other template engines we see fit.

It will be up to the developer working on the template to choose EJS or a different template engine if they see a better alternative. 

## **PNPM**

As with other repositories, integrations will also use **pnpm** instead of **yarn**.

## Extra

Some extra tasks to improve adapters that are considered “*nice-to-have*”:

- Remove tests and test files from the built `dist` folder
- Remove adapters off the internet and make them available only on **casgrain**

## Migration Plan

1. Move from **yarn** to **pnpm**
2. Introduce NX. It will be simply used to call `package.json` scripts (test, scratch and testgen), and `bb` commands (deploy, starterpack) at first

# Distributed Audit Trails

# Overview

This document references the distributed audit trails system, this system is designed to create a decoupled layer within our infrastructure in order to easily ingest changes across all our services. In turn providing a robust searchable api, that will allow systems to keep a historical record or track of any sort of changes.

| Reviewer | Status | Date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| @Dustin Blackman  | Reviewed | May 23, 2024  |
| @Jacob Cook  |  |  |
| @Mike  |  |  |
| @Augusto Bonifacio  | Reviewed | May 23, 2024  |

## Glossary

**Audit trails** - Is a collection of modifications done to a system

## Context

We see a surge in wanting to know who did what within our system, our current solutions are a bit opaque or not up to par, with issues in terms of a standardized way to keep track of things, in addition, building out the capabilities within the services.

The goal of this spec is to propose a distributed approach to audit_trails, this will allow any service to opt in across our microservices, with an exposed api to query whatever historical information is needed.

This will in turn reduce the effort needed to keep track of changes done by users by having to build out the audit trails per database or per table. Instead allowing a uniformed api to provide this data.

## Out of scope

Bigquery is a potential that can be used to scale even further or create aggregations for particular users. However, that is something more relevant for the future, it is perfectly fine to set it up via postgresql.

## High Level Overview

### Legacy

If we look at some of our historical approaches, especially in grand central we tend to see a common attempt to create audit trails. Though not wrong, they do not scale very well.

![Untitled](Distributed%20Audit%20Trails/Untitled.png)

Many of our historical records use this model, the problem with this is, it doesn’t scale, it doesn’t give a good point of reference and any new additions are manual. (this could technically be solved with triggers or other automation).

### Recent

In geo service we do have a more robust system, but there are issues with keeping track of the invoking user. However, at a high level this is what we want for most tables. As it can help us create logic to find the exact changes made within the system by a specific user.

![Untitled](Distributed%20Audit%20Trails/Untitled%201.png)

### Proposal

We want to move away from this as it can add a-lot of effort into the system, and standardizing it and making it easier to ingest, query and monitor database tables. In addition, developers tend to copy existing solutions without giving thoughts on its negative aspects. 

Which means that going forward, we move audit trails into a separate service that handles it, which will expose an api, allow clients to pass in data and allow services or clients to be able to see any changes through a single historical api.

The solution will be built by tackling the following areas

1. Database schema
2. API
3. Client Opt in

## Technical Design

### Database Schema

The approach that we can go for is of two folds. 

1. Dynamically generate tables on the fly with similar database structures for each unique table
2. Create a single uniform table

The more scalable approach may be generating the tables on the fly, as it can reduce search criteria's as data scales.

Audit trails don’t have to be complex, they just need the information available and the actions done. So the database schema can look like this.

```mermaid
erDiagram
    DynamicTable {
        string id "Unique identifier for each even"
        string event "Event type can be DELETE/UPDATE/INSERT"
        json previous "Serialized representation of the previous state"
        json new "Serialized representation of the new state"
        string token "Identifier for the user who made the change with the token"
        datetime created_at "Timestamp when the record was created"
        datetime updated_at "Timestamp when the record was last updated"
        json metadata "Additional metadata related to the event, this can be additional data we might want to attribute"
    }

```

This will have the baseline data in order to ingest which will help keep track of all the changes occurring within the system. 

We can then use the baseline data such as `token` to get the user who committed this action via il_controllorre. In addition, when we ingest the data we will store some quick lookups such as the user_id and author of the action (via token) and or api permissions sent by clients.

### API

The api will be responsible for getting data for a historical element or elements. The API will have pagination and the ability to filter data.

### Retrieve logs for all records in a table

`audit-logs.busbud-int.com/trails?table_name=geo_entity&limit=10` 

### Retrieve logs for specific record in a table

`audit-logs.busbud-int.com/trails?table_name=geo_entity&identifier=123&limit=10` 

### Response

Sample response, but can be adjusted easily. However, this can be easily integrated into our internal systems, such as back-office and finance dashboard. 

This will for example require a single UI component that will handle historical data, and can be used across various pages, significantly reducing waste and effort.

```jsx
[
    {
        "id": "36D7BACE-8B00-4112-903D-256C4347C749",
        "event": "UPDATE",
        "previous": {
            "name": "John Snow",
        },
        "new": {
            "name": "John Doe",
        },
        "author": "momo@momo.com",
        "created_at": "2024-05-22T08:00:00Z",
        "updated_at": "2024-05-22T09:00:00Z",
        "metadata": {
            "service": "geo_service",
            "permission": "geo-updates",
            "author": "mo"
        }
    },
    {
		    "id": "36D7BACE-8B00-4112-903D-256C4347C749",
        "event": "INSERT",
        "previous": null,
        "new": {
            "name": "John Snow",
        },
        "author": "yoyo@yoyoyo.com",
        "created_at": "2024-05-22T10:15:00Z",
        "updated_at": "2024-05-22T11:30:00Z",
        "metadata": {
            "service": "geo_service",
            "permission": "geo-create",
            "author": "mo"
        }
    }
]

```

### Ingestion

The goal of the system is to ingest the data via queues, so that we can scale the writes as we please. We don’t expect much traffic initially, it will entirely depend on adoption. However, writes don’t have to be a focus, we can maintain a certain throttle and threshold. The data will be ingested via Queues that will route to the audit logging service. If any issues pop up it will result in the data going to the dead letter.

### System Overview

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph RabbitMQ ["RabbitMQ"]
        Queue["Queue for Audit Trail Messages"]
    end

    subgraph Worker ["Worker"]
        Listener["Listener that ingests from RabbitMQ"]
    end

    subgraph API ["API"]
        API_SERVICE["AuditLog Service"]
    end

    subgraph DB ["Database"]
        Tables["Multiple Tables"]
    end

    RabbitMQ -->|Audit Messages| Listener
    Listener -->|Processes & Writes| Tables
    API_SERVICE -->|Publishes| RabbitMQ
    API_SERVICE -->|Reads/Writes| Tables

    style RabbitMQ fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style Worker fill:#ccf,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style API fill:#cfc,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style DB fill:#fcf,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px

```

## Risks

The biggest risk, is usually client adoption and any sort of intermediate network issues. However, this can be solved with the Queues and dead letters, that we can potentially leverage. The initial goal will be to at-least getting it to work with a couple services. The data and finance team is working on payouts solutions and we want to keep track of these changes as well.

The data is eventually consistent, meaning that the historical records are written async. Which is fine, because this is not crucial for its usage. Any UI or client can leverage the historical data for any part of their UI, as separate api calls, or aggregated for a specific service (the existing service makes an additional call to get audit data appended to its response).

## Rollout

The rollout will focus on the following, by creating a new project in auth-nest. This is normalized estimations across team members.

1. API (2 days - 1 week)
    1. This includes setting up the ingestion and all the api endpoints and it’s logic.
2. Integrate into other services (1 -2 days)
    
    We can integrate it into a subset of tables for grand central, but we will likely do it for finance first. As a test run, we might do it for `locations`, `cities`, `points-of-interests` as well as potentially `geo-service`. Though it’s already setup which may include migrating old data.
    

Client opt in will essentially be overwriting the hooks or triggers to pass in the data, which both prisma and sequelize support out the gate. So should be doable, we might also invest in a separate package that handles it as part of busbud service.

## Parties Involved

### Platform team

This initiative will be taken up by platform team member(s). Headed by @Muhammad Aqsam

# Interconnection Rules

| Reviewer | Status | Date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| @Dustin Blackman  | Under Review | 2025-04-08 |
| @Jacob Cook  | Approved | 2025-04-23 |
| @Rodrigo Alanis  | Approved | 2025-04-22 |
|  |  |  |

## Changelog

- `2025-04-08`: Add new `note` section for the rule editor
- `2025-04-17`: Add list of Github issues on the bottom
- `2025-04-17`: Add migration plan
- `2025-04-29`: Add modifier for number of returned interconnections
- `2025-04-29`: Deprioritize audit
- `2025-04-29`: Add section on migrating source’s `interconnection_enabled`
- `2025-07-14`: Update priority so that lower number means higher priority
- `2025-07-28`: Add `number_of_ics` rules

## **Introduction**

Operators are asking for more flexibility when it comes to Interconnections. We currently have hard coded rules to control which interconnections are allowed to generate.b

But the current approach doesn’t solve some of the business needs and also generates some problematic interconnections.

We want to add flexibility to control some parameters when generating interconnections depending on a certain set of conditions - to both address business needs and add flexibility to explore the current interconnection inventory.

## **Goal**

Create a system that allows us to easily modify a set of rules that control how and when interconnections are generated.

## **Glossary**

**IC**(s): interconnection(s)

# **Proposed Solution**

## **Overview**

The proposed solution consists of creating a new `InterconnectionRule` model that relies on **conditions** and **modifiers**.

This model will be used by Poll Service when generating ICs in order to either block or allow each IC from being generated. It will be saved on Grand-Central’s DB.

## Interconnection Rule

Each rule can be one of the following types:

- `allow`: allows every IC that matches the conditions to be generated
- `block`: blocks every IC that matches the conditions from being generated
- `modifier`: modifies the specified parameters (i.e. min and max transfer time) on ICs that matches the conditions
- `prioritize`: prioritize ICs that matches the conditions when choosing which legs to use
- `number_of_ics`: determine the number of interconnections to be cached

Rules have:

- `type`: (described above)
- `conditions`: an array of conditions that will trigger the rule (more below)
- `modifiers`: only when the type is `modifier`: an array of modifiers that modifies specified parameters (more below)
- `priority`: A priority number (from 1 to 1000*), where the smallest number is the higher priority (priority 1 takes precedence over priority 2)
    - User created rules start from 1 and end in 999, only the default rule can have priority 1000
- `state`: (to enable/disable the rule)
- `created_at`/ `updated at`

```tsx
interface InterconnectionRule {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  type: "allow" | "reject" | "modifier" | "prioritize" | "number_of_ics";
  conditions: InterconnectionRuleCondition[];
  modifiers?: InterconnectionRuleModifier[];
  priority: number;
  state: "active" | "disabled";
  created_at: string;
  updated_at: string;
}
```

## Interconnection Rule Condition

Each **condition** will also be a model saved on Grand-Central’s DB with a 1/n relationship with the `InterconnectionRule`.

Conditions have:

- `evaluation`: if we are checking for values that are in an array, or not in that array
    - For time related conditions, we should have `before` or `after` instead
- `property`: which IC property to look at
- `value`: array of strings
- `leg`: which IC leg to look for the value

Note that when the property is `same_transfer_station`, we don’t need to set a leg.

All conditions are evaluated as an `and` rule - all of them must match for the rule to be considered.

```tsx
interface InterconnectionRuleCondition {
 id: number;
 evaluation: "is in" | "is not in" | "before" | "after";
 property: "source" | "operator" | "same_transfer_station" | "arrival_time" | "departure_time" | "fare_xid" | origin_city | origin_country | destination_city | destination_country;
 values: string[];
 leg?: "1" | "2" | "any" | "all";
 rule_id: number;
}
```

When the rule type is `number_of_ics`, we can only have origin city and destination city as the condition properties; and there are no legs to determine since the rules will be applied per search instead of per trip combination.

## Interconnection Rule Modifier

Each **modifier** will also be a model saved on Grand-Central’s DB with a 1/n relationship with the `InterconnectionRule`.

Modifiers have:

- `type`: which interconnection parameter to modify
- `value`: string with the value (in some properties, it could be a number but it will be saved as string on the DB)

The type is based on the default config: https://github.com/busbud/poll-service/blob/e50204568c3b4805e0fe016609029041cd29e9cc/src/components/interconnection/domain/model/interconnection-filter.ts#L8-L17

```tsx
interface InterconnectionRuleModifier {
 id: number;
 type: "next_day_latest_departure_hour" 
     | "same_station_min_transfer_time_minutes" 
     | "different_station_min_transfer_time_minutes" 
     | "max_transfer_duration_hour" 
     | "nighttime_arrival_hour" 
     | "min_nighttime_transfer_time_hour" 
     | "max_distance_radius"
     | "distance_per_minute"
     | "number_of_ics";
 value: string;
 rule_id: number;
}
```

Note: we are adding a new `number_of_ics` modifier, which controls the amount of interconnections returned. This will require some updates on Poll-Service. This type of modifier is only available on `number_of_ics` rules.

## **Audit - deprioritized**

Note: we won’t need to work on this - as it will be worked on in the future by an audit framework.

Similar to Supply Rules, we want to keep track of updates on rules. 

For this, a new table will be created that will be updated with changes and which author performed them.

```tsx
interface InterconnectionRuleEdits {
 rule_id: number;
 previous_name: string;
 previous_type: "allow" | "reject" | "modifier" | "prioritize";
 previous_priority: number;
 previous_state: "active" | "disabled";
 previous_conditions: JSONB;
 previous_modifiers: JSONB;
 [updated_at: string;
 Updated_author: string;](../Guides & Checklists/Update Partner ID.md)
}
```

Conditions and modifiers will be saved as JSON properties on this table. There’s no need to create more tables for them.

## **Rule Priority**

### Rules of types `allow` , `block` , `modifier`

If multiple rules with the same type apply to the same IC, then the one with the highest priority should be used.

If multiple rules with different types apply to the same IC:

- If they are `allow` and `block`, then the one with highest priority should be used. If both have the same priority, then the `allow` rule will take precedence
- Other combinations of type will always be applied regardless of the priority number, since they are applied in different flows

If multiple rules have the same type and same priority number, then the oldest one should take precedence.

### **Rules of type `prioritize` / `number_of_ics`**

Today, after the trip legs are approved, we select the best ones based on the following conditions, where tie breakers move to the next condition:

- Earliest next leg (shortest transfer within requirements)
- Cheapest
- Same Operator
- Same Class

Rules of type `prioritize` will be used to sort the legs and those will be the first conditions evaluated when sorting legs. If multiple rules of type `prioritize` meet the conditions for an IC, then the one with highest priority should be taken into account first.

So, for example, if there are two rules, one with priority 5 and one with priority 10, the conditions list will be:

- Leg (or IC) that meets conditions for rule with priority 5
- Leg (or IC) that meets conditions for rule with priority 10
- Earliest next leg (shortest transfer within requirements)
- Cheapest
- Same Operator
- Same Class

## **Filtering Logic**

Interconnections can be filtered on three different steps:

1. When creating the **interconnection combinations**, which is when we check the routes that could be interconnections. The idea here is to filter what we can (using only the allow and block rules) to decrease the amount of ICs to be processed on next steps.
2. On **interconnection combination queue**: when we load the trips and save the hashes. 
    
    We have the trips, we could do some basic filtering using allow and block rules, to avoid extra processing on the next steps.
    
    [https://github.com/busbud/poll-service/blob/f6dff56112c87c7b149ebfadc9a47933fbd706f8/src/workers/interconnection/index.ts#L500](https://github.com/busbud/poll-service/blob/f6dff56112c87c7b149ebfadc9a47933fbd706f8/src/workers/interconnection/index.ts#L500)
    
3. On **interconnection poll**:
    
    This is where we assemble the interconnections, and where we should apply all rules:
    
    - A new filter will be created to `allow`/ `block` ICs based on the allow/block rules:  [GitHub](https://github.com/busbud/poll-service/tree/e50204568c3b4805e0fe016609029041cd29e9cc/src/components/interconnection/domain/service/filter)
    - Current filters will use the `modifier` rules to override the default values on current parameters: https://github.com/busbud/poll-service/blob/e50204568c3b4805e0fe016609029041cd29e9cc/src/components/interconnection/domain/model/interconnection-filter.ts#L8-L17
    - `Prioritize` rules will be used on to sort the IC when deciding which legs to prioritize: https://github.com/busbud/poll-service/blob/e50204568c3b4805e0fe016609029041cd29e9cc/src/components/interconnection/domain/service/sort/interconnection-sort-tracker.ts#L44

## **Default Modifier Rule**

Currently, we have default hardcoded parameters on Poll-Service. We can keep them there (with the exception of the `viarail`/ `riderexpress` rules) as fallback values if we ever need - but they should all be created as a `default` rule:

- It will have priority `1000` (all other rules have priority between 1 and 999) meaning any rule can override it.
- It will have no conditions, nor can it have conditions added to it.
- It cannot be disabled.
- Modifiers cannot be deleted but can be updated if needed.

So take the default parameters from:

[https://github.com/busbud/poll-service/blob/e50204568c3b4805e0fe016609029041cd29e9cc/src/components/interconnection/domain/model/interconnection-filter.ts#L8-L17](https://github.com/busbud/poll-service/blob/e50204568c3b4805e0fe016609029041cd29e9cc/src/components/interconnection/domain/model/interconnection-filter.ts#L8-L17)

We will create the following rule:

```json
{
 "type": "modifier",
 "name": "Default",
 "conditions": [],
 "modifiers": [
   {
     "type": "same_station_min_transfer_time_minutes",
     "value": "30"
   },
   {
     "type": "different_station_min_transfer_time_minutes",
     "value": "120"
   },
   ...
 ],
 "priority": 1000
}
```

Note that we currently have a few hardcoded rules (below). They will become new rules and won’t be hardcoded anymore. If any other hardcoded rules are created after this spec is writen, they should move to become Interconnection Rules.

- Block some sources (`viarail`, `viarail2` and `riderexpress`  - https://github.com/busbud/poll-service/blob/f6dff56112c87c7b149ebfadc9a47933fbd706f8/src/components/interconnection/domain/service/filter/has-compatible-source-on-each-leg-filter.ts#L14)
- Something with `ado` and `estrellablanca`: https://github.com/busbud/poll-service/blob/f6dff56112c87c7b149ebfadc9a47933fbd706f8/src/components/interconnection/domain/service/filter/has-compatible-source-on-each-leg-filter.ts#L20C7-L20C40

## **Grand-Central**

Grand-central will have new endpoints to create/update rules:

- `GET /interconnection-rules/`: Returns all interconnection rules
- `POST /interconnection-rules/`: Creates a new interconnection rule and returns the created rule
- `GET /interconnection-rules/<rule_id>`: Returns everything from given rule (including the conditions and modifiers)

- `GET /interconnection-rules/<rule_id>/edits`: Returns a list of all updates of that given rule

- Prevent creating/updating a rule of type other than `modifier` with modifiers
- Prevent disabling the default rule
- Prevent creating/updating rules with priority 1000 (other than the default one)

# Migration Plan

We want to migrate all current hardcoded rules to the new model in a way that we can track, compare and easily rollback if needed.

The implementation should include a feature flag and tracking in a way that we can run both “models” at the same time with a feature flag deciding which one to use for a final decision. 

This will enable us to run it for a week, compare the data and, if good, flip the switch. 

It’s strongly recommended to keep the feature flag and tracking for at least another week before removing the previous hardcoded rules; to make sure rollback is as easy as changing the feature flag.

### Sources `interconnection_enabled`

Sources currently have a `interconnection_enabled` flag. New rules should be created for each source where this is true, and the source column should be deprecated.
